one who desires splendor should worship that same number made from *kāśmīra* (saffron) [or produced from flowers].
In the spring, one should worship a liṅga produced from *madhupuṣpa* (the flower of the intoxicated bee).

One should worship [the deity] a hundred times. Every day, the practitioner becomes possessed of desire for a woman; however, the meditation here is as follows: one should constantly meditate upon Maheśa, who resembles a mountain of silver, adorned with the beautiful crescent moon, and whose limbs are radiant with jeweled ornaments.

Holding an axe, a deer, a boon-granting gesture, and the gesture of fearlessness in his hands, he is serene; seated upon a lotus, he is praised on all sides by hosts of immortals; wearing a tiger skin, he is the primordial source of the universe, worshipped by the universe, the remover of all fears, five-faced and three-eyed. 97.
One seeking the goal of the sacred fords (tīrtha) should worship two thousand authentic liṅgas.
In that regard, meditation is proclaimed separately for each of the bilva leaves. || 98 ||
May the beloved of the Daughter of the Mountain— the conqueror of the pride of Mada, who wears the king of serpents as a sacred thread, who moves with the gait of a white bull,
whose head is the lord of the night (the moon), and who is worshipped by Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Śiva, and others— grant us prosperity. 99.
"Yakṣakardama is produced from [the following]: saffron, agallochum, musk, camphor, and sandalwood;

it is called 'Great Fragrance' (mahāsugandha) by name, and is known as yakṣakardama"—thus says Dhanvantari. A thousand liṅgas increase one's devotion. One should make five thousand [liṅgas] made of jaggery.
For the increase of joy. || 100 ||
By worshipping a hundred thousand guḍaliṅgas, one shall become a king; by worshipping a thousand women, one shall become most beloved by her husband. (101)
By worshipping the lingas made of fresh butter, one obtains the highest fruit;
the same result is obtained from those made of ashes, cow dung, or sand. 102.
One who desires friends should worship [the deity] three thousand times month after month for one year with a steady mind; he becomes a friend of the world. || 103 ||
Whoever should worship eight hundred [times] every day for the duration of a month;
By the mere practice of the scriptures, one becomes even superior to the guru. || 104 ||
He who daily worships three liṅgas made of cow-dung in the morning, offering oblations of *bṛhatī* and *bilva* leaves and presenting jaggery as the food offering; || 105 ||
Doing this for three months, one obtains no small amount of wealth; he who worships eleven lingas made of cow dung [attains the same]. (106)
Morning, midday, evening, and at midnight—every day—if one should practice in this manner for six months, he shall attain all prosperity. || 107 ||
In any place whatsoever, for the purpose of deceiving thieves or even tax-collectors.
One should constantly worship the eight hundred Durbhūpas for three fortnights. || 108 ||
He who worships Śiva, born of cow-dung, with leaves produced from the picumanda tree (the nimba leaf),
and meditates upon Maheśvara as being enraged, conquers his enemies.
He who worships a thousand lingas made from ground turmeric shall, by means of five thousand [mantras], paralyze a sovereign lord of the earth. || 110 ||
One should constantly perform five hundred releases from fetters every month.
One who desires liberation from misfortune should perform five thousand [repetitions].
For the sake of liberation from imprisonment and other such constraints, the wise person should cause ten thousand [recitations] to be performed.
But one who is besieged by a great fortress shall obtain liberation within six months. || 112 ||
By worshipping ten thousand liṅgas, one shall remove the fear of a great king; or one should worship five hundred [liṅgas] every day for three fortnights. (113)
He who worships [the deity] two hundred times every day for one month has no fear of thieves; he returns from his country in safety. || 114 ||

In the event of fear from ḍākinīs and others, one should constantly recite [the mantra] seven thousand times; or if one worships it five hundred times for six months, that person shall be the ender of those [fears]. || 115 ||
If one worships five thousand [times] each month for five years, [the merit is as follows].
Or else, one is completely liberated from the poverty acquired in previous births. || 116 ||
One should constantly worship eleven lingas made of rice-flour;
within a single month, this shall burn away all impurity.
The man who, having properly fashioned a liṅga with black sesame seeds, should worship it;
For him, the destruction of all sins occurs after three years. || 118 ||
If a man worships a liṅga made from all kinds of flowers during the winter season, he shall become free from sin;
or likewise, if he should worship a crystal liṅga for three years.
For the sake of destroying the yoga of early widowhood, one should perform thirty thousand [recitations]; by ten thousand recitations at a linga, a maiden shall obtain a good husband. (120)
But for one who worships eleven lingas made of silver every day, all virtues arise and remain present for him. || 121 ||
Whoever worships ten thousand lingas made of sesame paste every day, or eleven [lingas] for the duration of a year,
shall become the lord of a village.
To avoid the loss of his Brahmanical status, he should worship a golden linga at the three junctions of the day, eating only at night and being devoted to the Rudra-hymns. || 123 ||
Whoever worships the liṅgas made of salt, whether combined or separately, their good fortune increases even if they are destitute. || 124 ||
He who, having made his food auspicious, should worship [the deity] for one ritual period—if he does so every day for a hundred times, his food shall become abundant in the field. || 125 ||
Or again, during the rainy season, one may worship ten thousand sugar-lingas.
One should worship eleven lingas made from dhattūra flowers.
Having fashioned ten thousand lingas made either from barley flour or from salt,
one shall bring the three worlds under one's control.
He who should worship three hundred separate [images] made from cow dung, [attains great merit].
Minor diseases shall be destroyed, and after six months, great maladies [shall likewise perish;
this is the remainder of the sense]. || 128 ||
The fruit of whatever action it may be does not arise merely by seeing it.
The fruits and the lingas are to be worshipped by him with a count of ten thousand.

Whoever worships the lingas with ten thousand blades of *dūrvā* grass or *guḍūcī*, there shall be the destruction of his premature death; likewise [the same result follows] from those made of *nīvāra* grain flour. (130)
He who worships a linga made of sapphire for six months, or alternatively a linga made of copper, attains prosperity. || 131 ||
But that linga which is made of crystal is called Yogeśvara; by worshipping it for a hundred thousand times, one shall attain the status of a lord of many. || 132 ||
Alternatively, for the sake of liberation from the house of the ancestors, or for the liberation of one's father, one should worship ten thousand silver lingas. || 133 ||
He who causes ten thousand golden liṅgas to be made attains Satyaloka by his mere resolve; of this there is no doubt. || 134 ||
One desiring long life should worship [an image of] a Naga, of lead, of tin, and of bell-metal;
for the sake of attaining bodily fragrance, one should worship an image made of sulphur. 135.
A poor man who worships even a single image made of wood from the first felling of a tree is liberated from poverty; he who worships a thousand such images is likewise freed from indigence. (136)
One desiring power should use that made from camphor, and one desiring wealth, that made from wheat flour.
The three—the Liṅga, the mudga-bean flour, and joy—should always be worshipped by the twice-born.
One who desires a thousandfold fragrance should always use that which originates from musk.
A linga made of ground black gram (māṣa) grants the constant attainment of food.
A Linga made of grain wards off the world of Yama;
a Linga made of Priyaṅgu-paste [or lead] is dear to all embodied beings. || 139 ||
He who performs [this rite] with white sesame seeds becomes the lord of Śvetadvīpa; having fashioned a liṅga of whatever is dear to someone, he shall obtain that very thing.
In the summer, however, he who worships ten thousand times with blossoms of the *mallikā* flower shall attain a form that is twice as beautiful. || 141 ||
Having fashioned a linga made of blue lotuses in the autumn, a person undoubtedly attains the fulfillment of whatever purpose they may have. || 142 ||
Having fashioned a beautiful liṅga with jasmine flowers in the winter season, the wise man who worships it with devotion rejoices together with Śiva. 143.
Among soft materials, the one made of earth is said to be the best;
among hard ones, stone is superior, and among stones, crystal is the most excellent. || 144 ||
From crystal [one obtains] ruby, and from ruby, saffron.
Then [the water] arising from rubies from Kāśmīra, and thereafter that produced from sapphires.
From indranīla comes gomeda; from gomeda, the origin of vidruma; from vidruma, the excellent pearl; and superior even to that is silver. (146)
Gold is superior to silver, and a diamond is better than gold.
Mercury is superior to diamond, and the Bāṇaliṅga is even more excellent than that.
Situated in the midst of the waters of the Narmadā, it is known as the Bāṇaliṅga.
The Liṅga worshipped by Bāṇāsura is called the Bāṇaliṅga. || 148 ||
When the self-manifested Bāṇaliṅga, which is like a moonstone, is situated in the heart.
The consumption of the food offering (naivedya) to Śambhu should be known as equal to the Cāndrāyaṇa penance. || 149 ||
This distinction between what is acceptable and what is unacceptable does not exist in the case of the Bāṇaliṅga;
the water and food offered to it may be accepted under the designation of *prāsāda*. (150)
The Liṅga consisting of the name of Śiva is always to be worshipped by the great sages; for it is considered the most worthy of worship among all Liṅgas. || 151 ||
An excellent liṅga is said to be four aṅgulas in height, beautiful, provided with a pedestal, and well-proportioned according to the five sūtras. || 152 ||
Half of that is declared the lowest; half of that again is remembered as the inferior. That which is less than this should never be used for worship, for it yields no true fruit. || 153 ||
A rudrākṣa and a śivaliṅga are both praised as they become increasingly large.
The Śālagrāma and the Narmada stone are subtle; the more subtle one is distinguished as superior. || 154 ||
Whether a Brāhmaṇa, a Kṣatriya, a Vaiśya, or even a Śūdra born in the natural order (anuloma).
One should constantly worship the Liṅga with devotion, using the respective mantra for each. || 155 ||

For Brahmins, worship with Vedic mantras alone is best; for those initiated into the Tantras, it is by the procedure prescribed in the Tantras. The worship of Śambhu is remembered as being performed according to the Smṛtis, and not by a non-Vedic path.
In those whose minds have been scorched by the curses of Dadhīci, Gautama, and others, faith in the pure Vedic rites will not arise. || 157 ||

That mortal who, disregarding both Vedic rites and likewise those prescribed in the Smṛtis, should perform other [practices], shall not obtain the fruit of his actions. Many will attain perfection in the Kali age through the earthen liṅga. 158.
In the Kṛta age, the liṅga is made of jewels; in the Tretā, it is made of gold; in the Dvāpara, the best is one of mercury; but in the Kali age, it is one of earth.
And with whatever offerings one has obtained, being endowed with devotion and faith.
A person should worship the earthen linga according to the procedure prescribed in the scriptures. || 160 ||
And one should not deliberate upon the investigation of the five threads before a king.
In whatever manner possible, one should fashion it according to the prescribed rule so that it is beautiful. || 161 ||
But one who divides it into two parts shall not obtain the fruit of worship at all.
It was produced from jewels, gold, coral, flour, and crystal.

The Liṅga may be made of a single block, as may other mobile and immobile objects; however, that which is of a single block is considered unstable, while that which is of two blocks is known as stable. || 163 ||
For Brahmins, the clay is white; likewise for Kshatriyas, it is reddish; for Vaishyas, it is yellow; and for Shudras, it is black, or whatever is available. || 164 ||
We meditate upon Mahādeva, who brings about existence and the destruction of existence; upon Ugra, the destroyer of the fierce;
and upon Śarva, whose crest is the moon. || 165 ||
This mantra has been proclaimed for the purpose of worshipping the *vilomas*;
then, upon the completion of the worship, one should offer three handfuls of flowers. || 166 ||
One should also perform the recitation (japa) of the five-syllabled mantra one hundred and eight times.
One should recite the praise that is about to be described for the satisfaction of the God.

Salutations to you whose nature is the syllable *oṃ*; [although there is elision according to the rule *yasya lopaś śākalyasya*, it is not considered non-existent by the rule *pūrvatrāsiddham* because this is Vedic usage; thus, by the rule *om-āṅośca*, the single substitute is the subsequent form.
Salutations to you who bear the body of the syllable *namaḥ*. Salutations to you, the self of *nāda*; salutations to you, the self of the *bindu* and *kalā* aspects.
Salutations indeed to the one whose form is both signless and possessed of signs, who has transcended all form. You are the mother of all worlds;
you alone are the father of the universe. || 169 ||
You are the protector, you are the well-wisher and friend, you are the beloved one assuming an auspicious form;
you are the teacher, you are the refuge, you are the witness, you are the father, and you are the grandfather. || 170 ||
Salutations to you, O Blessed Rudra, the Sun of immeasurable splendor! Salutations to the god Bhava, who is the embodiment of dharma and the source of welfare. 171.
Salutations to Śiva, the protector of the earth, who is ever fragrant; salutations also to the Lord of creatures (Paśupati), whose splendor is like fire and immeasurable. || 172 ||
Salutation to you, Bhīma, whose form is the sky and who consists of sound alone; salutation be to you, Mahādeva, Soma, and the Immortal. || 173 ||

Salutations to you, the fierce one, for the sake of the sacrificer; salutations to you, the practitioner of yoga through action. Salutations to you, O Oṃkāra, and to the one who has Dharma as his vehicle. || 174 ||
And by this worship of the earthen linga which has been performed by me, may the Blessed Lord Rudra grant my desired object. || 175 ||
Having thus offered praise, performed the recitation, and prostrated, one should dismiss [the deity].
Now, the ritual procedure for the eleven liṅgas is being described.
One should worship a single *liṅga* every day with the sixteen types of offerings; one should indeed worship it with *droṇa* flowers and offer ghee alone. || 177 ||

In this manner, by a hundred days, liberation from all debts is produced. One should worship the two Liṅgas every day with the sixteen types of offerings; for flowers, Mallikā blossoms are prescribed, and for the food offering (naivedya), jaggery is traditionally taught. || 178 ||

If one performs this for three hundred days, one shall obtain ten thousand sons; by performing it for three days each day with the sixteen modes of service (ṣoḍaśopacāra), [the same result is attained]. || 179 ||
One should present camphor as an offering along with karañja flowers; for five hundred days, a beautiful maiden shall appear. || 180 ||
One should perform the fourfold [service] every day with sixteen types of offerings.
One should worship with food offerings and campaka flowers.
Having performed [the rite] for five hundred days, marriage will certainly take place.
And one should offer an oblation of six sets of six bakula flowers, as well as honey alone. || 182 ||
Liberation from great strife shall come after three hundred days; one should worship with seven lotus flowers every day. || 183 ||
With curd-rice as the food offering for five hundred days, whatever sacred site is intended in the mind shall become that very place, and even the deity itself shall be present. (184)
But he who worships every day with eight bilva leaves, offering sweets as the food offering and the sixteen types of services; (185) p. 186).

By performing [this] for three hundred days, there shall be the attainment of the Great Knowledge (Mahāvidyā). By offering food oblations (naivedya) nine times every day for five months, [the same result is attained]. || 186 ||
With *bandhupuspa* flowers—[since it is stated in the lexicon that *bandhu* refers to the *bandhūka* flower, the meaning is *bandhujīvaka* flowers]—there shall be worship;
one will be freed from debt and become wealthy. [This should be done] ten times daily for one year.
With golden flowers. || 187 ||

There should be cakes for the purpose of the food offering (naivedya), and there may be travel to a distant land. Every day, the daily food offering should consist of eleven types of fivefold edible foods. || 188 ||
Flowers of the karavīra, gold, silver, and so forth.
And whatever he desires, such as pearls, coral, and so forth, that he shall obtain. || 189 ||

I shall describe the procedure for the concluding rite (udyāpana); one should perform it upon the completion [of the vow], when the worship of the Liṅga is finished, and when the desire has been fulfilled. || 190 ||
One should fashion a liṅga made of gold, silver, or even copper.
One should not practice stinginess regarding wealth; it should be prepared according to that [prescribed] measure.

This is the yoga known as Mahāśaiva; Ārdrā, Soma (Monday), and the fourteenth lunar day—when these two [or all three] coincide, it is Śaiva-yoga, and on such a single day, it is auspicious like Śiva himself. || 192 ||
The fruit of the Great Yoga (Mahāyoga) is abundant within the Śaiva Yoga; indeed, as it is stated in the Śivayoga, a human being attains that fruit. || 193 ||
Having fasted on the first day and having worshipped the Supreme Lord, as well as the preceptor and the Brahmins, one should then choose them for the purpose of the fire-oblation (homa). || 194 ||
Having worshipped Gaṇeśa and Ambā, and having established Śiva, one should worship him.
Having first performed the consecration of the vital breaths (prāṇapratiṣṭhā), one should carry out the installation of the fire.

One should also choose an Ācārya and officiating priests (Ṛtvij) by means of sacrificial fees (dakṣiṇā) and other gifts. One should perform as many fire-oblations (homa) as the number of Liṅgas one worships. || 196 ||
One desiring long life should offer ghee there, or one seeking wealth should offer milk-rice.
One should perform the oblation with sesame seeds and clarified butter; whatever else one may desire, that shall be distinct [from this].

One should keep a vigil at night accompanied by song and instrumental music; then one should perform the libation (tarpaṇa) and the ritual purification (mārjana), followed by the feeding of Brāhmaṇas. || 198 ||

For the satisfaction of Ambikā along with her attendants, he should give [the offering] to a group of young boys and maidens; then, having worshipped the liṅga once more, he should present it to his guru. || 199 ||

One should diligently please the preceptor with garments, ornaments, and other such gifts; having given abundant sacrificial fees (dakṣiṇā), one should partake of a meal together with one's friends. || 200 ||
Thus has been declared the supreme concluding rite (udyāpana) for the Linga; the procedure for earthen Lingas has been proclaimed as that which fulfills all desires. (201)
Together with the concluding rite (udyāpana), what else do you wish to hear? || 202 ||
Thus ends the ninth chapter, titled "Description of the Ritual for the Worship of the Earthen [Liṅga]," in the Merutantra composed by Śiva with the approval of the illustrious Mahāmāyā and Mahākāla.
The Śrī Devī said:
In some places it is Dakṣa, in some Vāma, and in some Saura and Śāmbhava.
In some places the Ūrdhvāmnāya is on the right, and in others it is on the north or the west.
Furthermore, there was the Āmnāyaka, the Gāṇapatya, and the Vaiṣṇava; in some places the Pārasīka, in some places the Buddhist, and here and there various heretical systems (pākhaṇḍa).
In one context you praise this or that, while in another you censure it; in some places you advocate a path devoid of a deity, and in others the Vedic Vedānta.
The religious duties of the islanders, the duties of the regions, and the duties of the lineages, here and there.
In various places, [he observed] the customs of regions, the customs of times, and the customs of castes.
If you are pleased with me, then tell me this supreme tantra;
speak the truth to me and make me free from doubt.
The illustrious Śiva said:
"Aho! The majesty of Time! Again and again you ask about its specific preeminence in various tantras;
I shall speak of that with pride."
This sattvic wisdom has arisen in you at this particular time; since you have asked for the sake of benefiting everyone, I shall speak that truth.
Just as a father's song is beneficial to a child, so too is the sound of the Vedas beneficial.
When ten thousand years of the Kali age have passed, || 8 ||
O Goddess, when the Veda, which is Nārāyaṇa himself, is no longer heard by living beings due to the divisions of time,
then it should be known that the [final] age has arrived.
Sounds such as speech, yawning, sneezing, and footsteps are subject to arising and perishing; likewise, let the deities understand that the scriptures are distinct from the Vedas.
As long as the circulation of this scripture exists in this world, indeed.
So long was that happiness for those on the path; now, however, the Vedic path has been blunted.
Therefore, those who practice that path are its disciples and its traditional successors.
They lead them onto their own path; as long as that [path] lasts, there may indeed be happiness. || 12 ||
Just as knowledge arises for men through the six sense organs, so too does the certain knowledge of the meaning of the Vedas arise through the six auxiliary sciences (ṣaḍaṅga). || 13 ||
Just as the organs of action of men are five in number,
so too have the five Āmnāyas of Kāla-Maheśa been declared by me.
The oral rite is declared to belong to that Ūrdhvāmnāya;
in this regard, the Vedas are the authority, as are the Smṛtis which are their constituent parts. (15)
His limbs are the Purāṇas; his deities are Gāyatrī and the others; he is born from the seed of Brahman; likewise, his field is the Brāhmaṇa woman;
and through the sacraments, he is considered a Brāhmaṇa, being consecrated by the rites of a Brāhmaṇa.
The conduct of a Brahmin is through the knowledge of Brahman; by that one becomes a Brahmin. He under whose control we are, and after whose word meaning follows, [is the true Brahmin]. (17)
If one characteristic is deficient, O Goddess, he pursues the meaning of speech; if two characteristics are deficient, he becomes a Brāhmaṇa by virtue of his own conduct. (18)
He who is devoid of the three characteristics attains accomplishment through the path of Tantra.
For those devoid of the four characteristics, there may be the Kaulika and other paths. || 19 ||
Distinguished by these characteristics, the collection of dharma should be performed according to place, according to family, according to caste, and according to time. || 20 ||
False speech and theft are censured on all paths.
Whatever birth, whatever action, no matter what recitation, austerity, or ritual deed [one may perform]. || 21 ||
One who is liberated while living is a speaker of truth, for everything is established in truth. Non-violence is the supreme dharma; that too [is practiced] through speech, body, and actions.
Where conduct is not rigid and caste is of no account, that place is like liberation; having enjoyed happiness in this world, one goes at the end to the supreme state. || 23 ||

Know him to be liberated while living—of this there is no doubt—even if he is liberated only at the time of death, provided that his mind is fixed upon that state which is free from causing distress to others. (24)
That creation which arises from sexual union possesses sensory perception;
he by whom that [creation] has been abandoned through the mind is indeed liberated while living. || 25 ||
Content with whatever is obtained by chance, he neither praises nor blames; he feels neither joy nor sorrow, and through such action, he is liberated. || 26 ||
Having abandoned the pleasures of the sense-objects and established himself in supreme contentment, he should spend as much time as is required for the maintenance of the body. || 27 ||
Free from desire, anger, and other such passions, he performs austerity in solitude; indeed, he who desires no fruit whatsoever is truly one liberated while living. 28.
The wife of Mahākāla is difficult to discern and difficult to ward off.
If she herself, being pleased by the worship of her own portion, releases him; || 29 ||
Just as a mother is deceived by her beloved sons of clever intellect, so too is this [mind] deceived;
he who is thus deceived is called one liberated while living (jīvanmukta). || 30 ||
Food, drink, and sexual intercourse have been made into a means of bondage by her; he who understands this in such a way shall then become liberated from bondage himself.
The gods desire worship; therefore, they are bound by their attachment to possessions.
He who does not accept gifts like a parrot is indeed some rare one liberated while living.
For one who constantly regards the body as excrement while performing service to Śauri, the conceit of "I am the body" has fallen away;
he alone is truly liberated while living.
This indeed is the easy path; there is no need for deliberation here. He who brings everything to completion through the study of the Veda is one who attains liberation. || 34 ||
"Who is the agent seen here? What is this? And where does it go within the mind?"—contemplating thus constantly, one should attain dissolution in Mahākāla. (35)
Therefore, [it is not to be practiced] by the Vāmikas, the Kaulikas, or those who are ignorant, and without a Guru.
Whether by all [the causes] together or by some unknown ones, she has been deceived, and not by others. || 36 ||
One who meditates upon Mahākāla shall have his bonds broken and his fetters severed;
he then becomes liberated while still alive (jīvanmukta). || 37 ||
The various modes of bondage and liberation have been compiled by me in this tantra.
By those who have known it through the path of the Guru, this bondage has been liberated. || 38 ||

Those who abandon their own duty (svadharma) because of the words of a bad teacher, or from a mere semblance of knowledge derived from a book, and remain submerged therein—they are truly lost. || 39 ||

Therefore, I shall proclaim the Dharma for those who possess wealth and authority—those for whom there may be both worldly enjoyment and liberation, as well as those for whom there may be a miserable rebirth. (40)
Disciples who possess the capacity for learning must certainly be instructed; by doing so, the teacher gains spiritual luster, and the disciple also attains happiness. || 41 ||
Furthermore, he who out of delusion or greed should bestow initiation upon one who is unqualified shall become impoverished, and his disciple shall become a vessel of suffering. (42)
If even one of the previously mentioned characteristics is not seen in a Brahmin, he will surely cause some affliction,
despite having attained the status of a Brahmin.
"No qualification for any of the rites pertaining to Brahman has arisen for me; how shall I obtain happiness in this world or in the next? (44)
He who is blind toward the property of others, who is impotent toward the wives of others, and who is mute toward the slander of others—one should always reflect in this manner. || 45 ||
In this matter, that very Brāhmaṇa possesses the qualification for Brāhmaṇahood; whereas those who are not Brāhmaṇas, whoever they may be, say, "We are devoted to meat and liquor. || 46 ||
"Devoted to the thought, 'How may we obtain liberation?'"
Those who possess the characteristics previously described are also proclaimed to be disciples.
He who is endowed with the five characteristics is indeed the Brāhmaṇa, who is Time itself; I, Brahmā, and likewise Viṣṇu, abide under the power of his command.
If he reaches the path of the left, he is born again even as a dog.
A Brahmin endowed with four characteristics should be known as mediocre. || 49 ||
If, due to the power of misfortune, some Tantric mantra is bestowed by those two upon someone,
it bears fruit immediately for the first person, but through the ritual practice of the other.
For one who possesses the three characteristics, both the Vedic and Tantric [paths] yield results through the practice as prescribed; this is not the case for the Vāmaka.
Both his left and right [hands], when endowed with the two characteristics, shall yield results equal to the mind;
never, however, does the Vedic [method] do so.
Endowed with a single characteristic, his left [hand] bestows the fruit.
The accomplishment of those ranging from Śūdras to Yavanas is established in the Left Path (Vāmapatha).
A Brahmin who stands on the path of the left-hand way (vāmamārga) shall never touch tulasī;
he shall not touch a Vaiṣṇava Brahmin, nor shall he bow down to one who follows the Vedic path.
Even a base Brahmin, Kshatriyas and others, or even those devoted to the path of the Left (Vāmamārga), [are not excluded].
Because they follow that path, they are likewise purified by the vows of Viṣṇu and freed from all sin.
You would have proclaimed the Dharma openly, which brings happiness to those who follow the left-hand path.
Association with the virtuous, solitude, and two steady eyes. (56)
How can even the other [the wife] obtain happiness from one who has no regard for anyone else? (p.
190) To one who is attached to worldly pleasures and claims, "I am a knower of Brahman," [one should respond: 57.
One should abandon that which is ruined by both karma and Brahma, like one who has gone astray; likewise, [one should avoid] liquor, meat, the drinking of wine, fish, women, and kinsmen. 58.
Where many [beings] are born, there the left [nostril] grants movement; but having stayed upon the right path, meat and other such things are secretly enjoyed. || 59 ||
He goes to a terrible hell and is born as a worm in excrement; therefore, the collection of Vedic dharma should always be practiced by the twice-born. || 60 ||
He who eats meat without an offering, drinks liquor without worship, or approaches the wife of another without performing the sacrifice of the *dūtī*, is a denizen of hell. || 61 ||
If one who is ignorant of the conduct of the *samaya* and the family law (*kuladharma*) should practice it, both that teacher and that disciple shall become a beast for the *yoginīs*. (62)
He who, ignorant of the left-hand path (vāmamārga), yet aspires to liberation,
is like one who wishes to cross the shoreless ocean from this side to the other using only his two arms.

Those who are devoid of all ritual actions and have abandoned the system of castes and stages of life (varṇāśrama)—whether they follow the Kaula path or the Vāma path—are the recipients of both worldly enjoyment and liberation. || 64 ||
"Let all my kinsmen revile me; let my sons and others abandon me; let people laugh at me upon seeing me, or let kings punish me. (65)
Even though I am constantly tormented by disease, poverty, suffering, and the like;
Let Lakṣmī stay or let her go; I shall not abandon these paths.
Thus, he whose devotion is firm shall attain accomplishment even through the left-hand path.
Neither out of greed for wealth, nor out of anger, nor out of hatred, nor out of envy. || 67 ||
One should not abandon the path one has attained out of desire or even out of fear; nor should one fail to worship the Goddess every day, for in this path one would encounter obstacles. 68.
For he who is purified by the compassion of the Guru, whose bodily impurities have been shaken off, and who is devoted to the worship of his lineage—he is a Kaula, and no other. || 69 ||
Who can authorize what is beyond the senses, and for whom will what come to pass? Or rather, the vision of the Supreme Deity is that which yields its fruit directly before one's eyes.
Some claim that those who lack the instruction of a guru are great; others, having been deluded themselves in the past, delude the people. (71)
Drink, wine, meat, food, and the pleasure of a beloved wife—having perceived these [as impermanent].
Such indeed is the conduct that has been proclaimed, and so do the common folk proclaim.
If sages were to attain perfection through the drinking of liquor, then why would all those who delight in drinking liquor not become perfected beings? (73)
If a meritorious destiny were to result from the mere act of eating meat, then there would be liberation for carnivorous beasts, for they eat nothing other than meat. (74)
O gods, if liberation were produced through sexual union with women, then everyone would be liberated; who then would be born again? (75)
The approach of the sword's edge and the hanging from a tiger's ear.
Indeed, the serpent-enclosure can certainly be overcome by following the path of one's lineage. || 76 ||
O Goddess of gods, drinking [liquor] in vain is here called *surāpāna* (drinking liquor); that is to be known as a great sin (*mahāpātaka*), as described in the Vedas and other scriptures. || 77 ||
Wine and the meat of animals are unfit to be smelled, unfit to be seen, and certainly unfit to be drunk;
yet for the Kaulikas, they yield great fruit.
Indeed, there are eleven kinds of intoxicants that are impure for the twice-born;
however, the twelfth, the spirituous liquor known as *surā*, is traditionally held to be the most forbidden of all.
Therefore, a Brahmin, a Kshatriya, and a Vaishya must not drink liquor.
Upon merely seeing liquor, one should gaze at the sun.
Merely by contact with that liquor, one should perform three breath-restraints (prāṇāyāmas).
If [the water] reaches the knees, it constitutes a bath; if it reaches the navel, one should fast for a day.
If one touches liquor above the navel, the rule is a fast of three nights; if the drinking of *surā* has been committed, one should cause a blazing iron staff to be thrust [into the mouth]. 82.
When his mouth has been thus consumed by fire, he shall attain purification. O beloved, he who kills living beings for his own sake by means of a blow— || 83 ||
A person of evil conduct shall dwell in a terrible hell for as many days as there are hairs on the body of a beast,
and is thereafter born among the animal species.
The one who consents, the one who divides, the one who slaughters, the buyer and the seller, the one who prepares the food, and the one who eats—these eight share equally in the act. || 85 ||

One who kills after purchasing [the victim] with wealth is the "consumer"; one who eats [the flesh] is the "enjoyer. The "slayer" is considered the first type, involving killing, binding, and so forth; thus, the killer is regarded as being of three kinds. || 86 ||
One should never cut even grass except according to the prescribed rule; by killing a cow or even a twice-born man in accordance with the rule, one is not tainted by sin.
The Kaulika is superior to all, as is the follower of the Upper Tradition (Ūrdhvāmnāyin) and the Vāmaga.
The qualified person is one who is endowed with devotion and is a servant of the guru. || 88 ||

In the Western Tradition (Paścimāmnāya) there is withdrawal (saṃhāra), while in the Northern Tradition (Uttara) there is grace (anugraha). They know Mantra-yoga to be the Eastern [Tradition], but Bhakti-yoga is the Southern [Tradition]. (89)
The yoga of action is the western one, and likewise, the yoga of knowledge is the northern one.
In the location of the Mātṛkā-nyāsa, on the left, in the path of the Kaulikas. || 90 ||

One should perform the ritual deposition (nyāsa) known as the "Yoga of Elaboration" (prapañcayoga); that is thus described. [It is performed] in the Śrīprapañca, the Dvipamāyā, and likewise in the Kamalājaladhi. || 91 ||
And at Giriviṣṇuvallabha, there is the city of Padmadhariṇī.
On the seat of the Daughter of the Ocean (Lakṣmī), she is the Mother of the World in the pair of sacred fields.
Vana and Kamalavāsinī, as well as Indirā and Āśrama;
likewise, Ramā and Guhya, and Padmā and Caranakau. (93)
Nārāyaṇapriyā and Udbhijjā possess two Lakṣmīs; [the goddess] accompanied by Svedajā possesses three. Mahālakṣmī possesses four, while Jarāyujalakṣmikā possesses five. (94)
In the place of the vowels there are sixteen pairs; then, among the consonants (sparśakas), there are Āryā, Lava, Truṭi, and Caṇḍikā, accompanied by their respective measures (kalās). 95.
In the Kāṣṭhādurga, which is called Nimeṣa-śiva, the breath is indeed Aparṇikā.
Ambikāghaṭikā, as well as the Muhūrta joined with Satī. || 96 ||
Īśvarī is indeed Praharā, Śāṅkarī is conjoined with the day (divasa), Īśānī is Sandhyā, and Pārvatī is joined with the night (rātri). || 97 ||
Thereafter, one should deposit the state associated with Sarvamaṅgalā.
Likewise, one should place ten thousand offerings for Dākṣāyaṇī and Haimavatī on their respective days.
Then one should assign the asterism conjoined with Mahāmāyā, as well as the *yoga*, the *karaṇa* with Māheśvarī, and the lunar fortnight with Mṛḍānī. || 99 ||
Rudrāṇī is conjoined with the month, and Śarvāṇī is conjoined with the zodiacal sign.
Then there are Kālī and Ṛtuparameśvarī, joined with the two solstices (ayana). || 100 ||
One should place Kātyāyanī, Vatsarā, Gaurī joined with Yuga, Bhavānī, and Pralaya in the positions beginning with the east. || 101 ||
Brahmī is endowed with the five elements; Vāṇī is then Vāgīśvarī, conjoined with the five subtle elements and possessed of the five organs of action. || 102 ||

She is the goddess Sāvitrī endowed with the subtle organs of perception, Sarasvatī accompanied by the vital breath (Anila), Gāyatrī possessed of the [three] qualities, and she is united with speech and the internal organ (antaḥkaraṇa). || 103 ||

One should install the pervasive [deities] with the Vidyā-mantra: Śāradā conjoined with the states (avasthā), Bhāratī conjoined with the elements (dhātu), and Priyā conjoined with the humors (doṣa). || 104 ||
At the end of the three-syllable root-vidyā, following the letters of the Mātṛkā alphabet.
One should say "Salutation to Śrī, whose form is conceptual proliferation," in due order. || 105 ||
One should, however, apply the method of the final phoneme enriched by the emanations and so forth.
Immediately thereafter, [one should perform the placement] in the locations prescribed for the Mātṛkā-nyāsa.

One should perform the pervasive placement (*vyāpaka-nyāsa*) by uttering the salutation "Obeisance to the Noble Mother Parāmbā" to this very phenomenal world (*prapañca*), which has the three *tāra* mantras as its root, according to its true nature. (107)
The ritual deposition of the manifold (prapañcanyāsa) is thus completed; now the ritual deposition of the worlds (bhuvananyāsa) is described.
And at the end of the three-syllable root mantra, the letters [should be placed] according to their respective divisions. || 108 ||
Having pronounced [the names] along with the anusvāras, and having uttered the names beginning with Bhūtala, one should say "koṭi" at the end of the hundred worlds; this is the secret word. || 109 ||
Then, having uttered "Salutation to the Goddess Ādhāraśakti," who is the primordial deity of the Yoginīs, one should perform the ritual placement (nyāsa) upon the aforementioned limbs. 110.
The division of the syllables consists of three triads beginning with 'A'. Then, joined with the half-moon (bindu), there are two [syllables] in each of the two positions. 111.
The seven groups beginning with 'ka' and fourteen lakhs [of verses]; then the names of the worlds: Atala and Vitala. (112)
Sutala, Mahātala, Talātala, Rasātala, and Pātāla;
as well as Bhūr, Bhuvaḥ, Svaḥ, Mahar, Janaḥ, and Tapaḥ. (113)

And then there is Satya; furthermore, it is said to be located in the secret place (guhya) and so forth. Then there is the second, the inner secret (guhyāntara), and the inconceivable, supreme secret (atiguhyam). 114.
The great secret, independent, and the supreme secret foremost; the syllable Oṃ in the abode of the Yoginīs, the secret knowledge foremost. (115)
Having spoken of the secret and the ritual action, it is then applied in the eighth [chapter]:
the secret is Ḍākinī, and the great secret is Hākinī. (116)
Mahāgupta and Kākinī are more secret, while Śākinī is even more secret; thereafter come the secret Śrī-Hākinī, Mahākāya, and Yākinī. 117.
One should perform the placement (nyāsa) in due order: the two ankles, the hips and knees, the thighs and ankles, as well as the mūlādhāra, the svādhiṣṭhāna, and the navel.
The heart, shoulders, throat, forehead, and the aperture of Brahma (brahmarandhra) are, in this order, [the locations].
At the end of the three-syllable root mantra, one should utter "vaṃ" fourteen times.

One should place the heart-mantra pervading the heart of the Goddess, the Supreme Mother (Parāmbā), who is the sovereign ruler. I shall now describe the ritual placement of the forms (mūrtinyāsa); first, therein, are the three *praṇavas*.

Having recited the root mantra, one should perform the ritual placement (nyāsa); that is now described. One should duly place [the mantras] upon the limbs as previously stated, joined with the dative case ending and the word "namaḥ. || 121 ||
Māna at the beginning, and Priya at the end; Keśava on the head, and Ākṣaya on the face;
Nārāyaṇa on the lips (the lengthening is according to Vedic usage), and Mādhava on the right shoulder.
Govinda is accompanied by Īśānī on the left, and he is joined by Ugrā; Viṣṇu is in the upper eye, while Madhusūdana is on the right side. || 123 ||
And on the left side is Ṛddhi, while Trivikrama is on the right hip.
On the left hip of Rukmiṇī is Vāmana, endowed with splendor.
The two who uphold wisdom are on the right thigh, while the two who are mines of faults are situated on the left arm.
Ekanāsa and Hṛṣīkeśa he should place upon the right knee. || 125 ||
Ekāriṇī should be on the left thigh of Padmanābha, and Oghavatī on the right; Dāmodara is on the right shank, joined by Vāsudeva on the left.
Then, on the left shank of Ānāthā, there is Añjanaprabhā.
Joined with Saṅkarṣaṇa on the right foot, she is joined with Pradyumna [on the left].
A garland of bones is on the left foot, and Aniruddha is conjoined with the Earth (L). These sixteen [syllables] are to be placed, preceded by the nasalized vowel (Anusvāra) and so forth. || 128 ||
This assignment (nyāsa) is proclaimed for those endowed with devotion to Viṣṇu. In the Śaiva nyāsa, Karabhadra and Abhava are considered to be on the right foot. || 129 ||
On the left are Khaga, Balā, and Śarva; Gati-dā and Phala-prada; [the pair] Ṛddhi and Dakṣa;
and Īśāna, who is endowed with the station of the world. || 130 ||
One should likewise place them in sequence: Tatpuruṣa and Uḍuvallabha; Aghora and Jñānanādī; and then Ṭaṅka joined with Dharā. (131)
Then there are Vāmadeva and the one called Sadyojāta, along with Jaṣṭaṅka, Dhara, and Dāminī; here, moreover, the Brāhma-nyāsa should be performed, and Brahmā and Pakṣiṇī reside in the foot. 132.
Then Prajāpati and Rañjanī are on the two shanks; next, Vedhas and Lakṣmī are on the two knees;
and Sraṣṭṛ and Haritānanā are on the two thighs. || 133 ||
One should place Lalitā on the forehead and likewise Caturānana; one should then install Kṣamā and Hiraṇyagarbha in the aperture of Brahmā (the crown of the head).
At the end of the three-syllable root mantra, one should utter the word "Śrītrimūrti."
And one should perform the pervasive [prostration] with a salutation to the noble mother-goddess Aparāmbā. || 135 ||
Having thus performed the rite of ritual placement (nyāsa), one should perform the recitation (japa) and other practices.
And that practitioner of recitation is not at all afflicted by spirits, ghosts, people, and the like. || 136 ||

Now I shall state, according to the Vāmācāra tradition, the characteristics of the vessels and other implements; for without a support (ādhāra), the Mothers do not find satisfaction in their portions. (137)
Having four feet, three feet, six feet, or being circular—thus the characteristics of the vessels for the castes beginning with the Brahmins are described. || 138 ||
[The water] produced from coconut, gold, starfish, pearl-oyster shells, and stone.
[The vessels] made of conch, bell-metal, wood, tortoise shell, skull, gourd, or clay. || 139 ||

The [qualities] of Brahmins and the other castes are proclaimed as superior, middling, and inferior. One should avoid [a blade] that is not too thick, not too fine, and that is neither cut nor split. (140)
One should not have a vessel made of metals such as copper or bell-metal; for the attainment of Brahman occurs through gold, while the end of suffering is achieved through a vessel of silver.
Peace is obtained from a stone slab, while a pillar made of clay or coconut shell brings subjugation and other powers;
knowledge is gained from a tortoise-shell, and a mother-of-pearl shell bestows liberation. (142)

A rosary made from the wood of a sacred tree destroys sins, while one made of clay provides a means of livelihood. Success for a hero is achieved with a skull, and the attainments of yoga are gained with a gourd.
There should be twelve prasthas of water and four prasthas of rice.
Having cooked half a *prastha* of rice until it is as beautiful [in appearance] as that [quantity],
one should let it sit for two days in a place free from cold and other such elements; thereafter, placing it over the fire,
one should cook it until it resembles mud (*jambāla*).
One should place a quarter-prastha of beautiful rice grains of that same measure.
Having left it for two more days, one should again arrange it in this manner.
Having taken the *arka* [juice], one should pour it well into rice; having performed this three times in the same manner, it is known as *tāṇḍulīyā* liquor. || 147 ||
This very one shall be Soma, the bestower of the fruit of the Soma sacrifice. In the Dūtī-yāga, when the union occurs, that is traditionally known as the drinking of Soma. || 148 ||
The destination that belongs to those Kaulikas who do not perform the Soma sacrifice, as well as their enjoyment and heaven, comes to these Vāmins without any hardship. || 149 ||
Thus, that which arises from barley flour is known as *yavasoma*; by the combination of barley and rice, it is called *śaktisoma*. (150)
Wheat that has been steamed and ground, combined with ginger in equal measure,
should be kept for twelve days, surrounded by *vāruṇī* wine.
That liquor, known by the name Sūrya, increases the intoxication of the Yoginīs;
when drunk at the conclusion of the Cakra worship, it bestows the fruit of the Vājapeya sacrifice. || 152 ||
This very leaf, prepared in three ways along with wine, becomes fire;
by drinking it, one obtains the fruit of offering a fire-sacrifice. || 153 ||
When fire has been placed within the Vāruṇī apparatus for seven days, [it becomes a great success].
This [mantra] named Pacedanalā is the destroyer of great sins. || 154 ||
Ten *prasthas* of jaggery are prescribed, and an equal amount of bark from the *babbūla* tree.
Jambu bark and ghātakī flower [are used], and half as much of that which is produced from coconut. 155.
The *kusuma* measure should be half of that, and the *harītakī* measure should be half of that.
Vibhītaka is said to be that much [in quantity], and the three pungents (kaṭutraya) should be one-fourth part. || 156 ||
At that time, twelve parts of jaggery should be added to that *citraka*; one should then properly rotate it with the hand in both forward and reverse directions. (157)
By performing one hundred and eight repetitions at each of the three junctions of the day every day, purification occurs within twelve days;
one should cook it using the Vāruṇīyantra.
This is renowned as Gauḍī, considered to be highly intoxicating;
it was created by Śiva in the past and drunk himself by the Bhairavas. (159)
One should add water twice the amount of the flower-nectar to the jaggery; the cooking will be complete in sixteen days, while the rest is as previously described. (160)
This is beloved by all the gods and is the supreme means of subjugation; even the powers of the gods are brought under control—what need then to mention human women? || 161 ||
Harītakī, citraka, marica, and likewise dhātakī, along with madhūkapuṣpa and honey, should be increased by one part each. || 162 ||
The remainder, mixed with eighty jujube fruits, is as before. This captivating liquor is the supreme drink for the Yoginīs. (163)
O gods, I shall now describe the state of intoxication that accomplishes the *bindu*:
buffalo curd should be taken along with four hundred times its weight of molasses. (164)
Likewise, the juice of ripe, crushed plantain fruit should be taken;
with one-fourth part of curd added, it should be rubbed together and placed in a jar. || 165 ||

This [prohibition] is even more praiseworthy for Brahmins than the prohibition of *surā* itself. *Surā* is traditionally known to be of three kinds: that made from molasses (*gauḍī*), that made from honey (*mādhvī*), and that made from flour (*paiṣṭī*). (166)
This [practice] is appropriate for Śūdras, but it would not be so for Kṣatriyas or Vaiśyas.
The wine of the bliss of Brahman was drunk by those brahmins who were Kaulikas.
For them, wine does not cause madness; rather, it is said that the contemplation of Brahman increases their intelligence. Thus has it always been the opinion of the virtuous.
If a brahmin should have the habitual tendency toward liquor and intoxicants, [he is fallen].
He should be excluded like a Cāṇḍāla; he is neither a Vāmī nor a Kaulika.
The deities reside in the mouths of the Vāmins and the Kaulikas;
they carry that fragrance [to others], and such a twice-born man shall be worthy of worship. (170)
He in whose mouth there is no deity is indeed a caṇḍāla in person. The liquor made from flour (paiṣṭī) bestows all perfections, while that made from molasses (gauḍī) grants enjoyment. 171.
Honey is known to grant liberation, while grapes are considered to bestow sovereignty.
The Ikṣuvī is said to bestow knowledge, while the Khārjūrī destroys enemies.
The one born from the palmyra palm is praised for immobilization; the one called from the jackfruit tree bestows auspiciousness; that produced from the coconut grants prosperity;
and the one born from the neem tree destroys disease. (173)
That which is born from the Madhūka tree is known as Jñānakarī; Maireya is the destroyer of sin. That which is joyful, appetizing, fragrant, and captivating [is the wine]. || 174 ||

That liquor is supreme, O Goddess, as it causes delight to the deities. One should mix the liquor, meat, and Vijayā with the eight fragrances; having kneaded them, one should form pills as before and offer them into the water, thereafter performing worship. 175.
Dhattūra seed, Vijayā, Jātī leaf, and likewise its fruit; Akārakarabha and the bark of the Vatsa tree. || 176 ||
Having ground liquor with a portion increased by one-eighth part and formed it into pills, this drop, known as the "Eight Fragrances," is dear to the deity. || 177 ||
The assembly of Brahmins should perform the worship with buttermilk mixed with jaggery and likewise with honey;
one must not omit this rite.

If one should omit [the rite] through negligence, one would incur the curse of the deities. Alternatively, one should perform the libation with the juices of Vijayā, or in their absence, with water. || 179 ||
Just as one who has consumed opium becomes distressed without it, so too are the mantra-deities of the Kaulika women afflicted by exhaustion [without them]. 180.
For indeed, [the deities] afflict the practitioner if he is without liquor and meat; yet, without those two, the mantras grant enjoyment to their devotees. (181)
They arise indeed fruitless and cause the practitioner to wander; therefore, even the lowly do not fall into the left [path] when there is discernment. 182.
Meat is said to be of three kinds, arising from those that move in the air, on the earth, and in the water; one should employ each according to its availability for the purpose of satiation. 183.
One should likewise kill the animal after consecrating it with this mantra.
Worship with perfumes, flowers, and unbroken grains; otherwise, one shall go to hell. || 184 ||
This *piṇḍa* has been made auspicious; therefore, you have attained the state of Śiva. Arise, O bound soul (*paśu*), for you are not inauspicious—you are indeed Śiva! || 185 ||
Brahmā resides in water, Viṣṇu in fragrance, and Rudra arises from that; the Supreme Self (Paramātman) resides in bliss. Therefore, O beloved, this [bliss] is to be cultivated. 186.
In the absence of meat, however, one may use garlic, fresh ginger, or dry ginger;
or likewise, onions, meatballs, and lentils. || 187 ||
One should satisfy [the deity] even with liquor that is devoid of fish and meat;
however, one should not perform worship with material offerings lacking both meat and fish. 188.

Even if one possesses flesh, sesame seeds, and entrails, if one lacks even half a sesame seed’s worth of the *bindu*, humans will not attain the state of a deity; otherwise, they are merely the manifestation of a *preta*. (189)
It should be drunk by Brahmins, Kaulikas, and all Kshatriyas when the battle arrives.
It should be drunk by Vaiśyas at the time of sacrificing a cow, and by Śūdras during sexual intercourse with a woman. || 190 ||
Having worshipped the gods and the ancestors according to the path prescribed in the Śakti scriptures, one who drinks liquor and eats meat while remembering the Guru incurs no fault. || 191 ||

For the sake of steadying the meditation on Brahman and as a cause for the satisfaction of the deities, one may consume honey and meat; yet if it is for his own gratification, he is a sinner. || 192 ||
By consuming substances such as fish, meat, and fat outside of the time for sacrifice, one becomes a perpetrator of a great sin (mahāpātakin). || 193 ||
Just as the drinking of Soma by the learned brahmins during sacrifices is not censured, so too the drinking of wine by the Kaulas at the conclusion of worship is not condemned. 194.
Having correctly understood [this] from the Kula scriptures of the venerable Guru, the five mudrās are performed by the practitioner;
otherwise, he shall fall [from his state]. || 195 ||
By drinking [alcohol] without performing the ritual repetition, devotion to the guru, worship of the gods and others, and the festival of the heroes, one incurs the curse of the deities. || 196 ||
O Goddess, when your body was cast off at Dakṣa’s sacrifice, I took it upon my shoulder and prepared to wrap it in the funeral pyre. || 197 ||
Wherever he went for the purpose of entering the submarine fire, there he was quickly extinguished by Śakra with waters. || 198 ||
As I wandered in this manner for a year, great perspiration arose within me.
Then this earth became completely consumed by the falling of those drops.
Then Viṣṇu was entreated for the protection of the Earth;
he himself, with light arrows, pierced your limbs. (200)
Having divided [the earth] into eighty-four segments, he cast it down upon the ground; then, afflicted by the wind, I went forth as the entirety of Dharma.
Viṣṇu, having manifested himself, fell at my feet; having raised me up and embraced me, your grief was forgotten.
Then Brahmā and the other gods, as well as Nārada and the great sages, offered hymns of praise; at that time, O Pārvatī, Viṣṇu spoke these words.
O Maheśa, you who possess the light of knowledge, how have you fallen into delusion, desiring to enter the fire along with the bodies of these virtuous women? || 204 ||
"A woman should follow her husband, but a man does not go after her"—disregarding this scripture, O Lord, how have you been so deluded? (205)
When the Lord of Gods had spoken thus, they addressed me and Hari with words full of double meaning, yet their limbs remained true to this earth. (206)
Due to contact with corpses here and there, that earth was devoid of brahminical rites; [he sought] the purification of that ground as well as the purity of the brahmins. (207)
"Act in such a way that the word of Brahmā becomes true. Then, having meditated and having obtained the consent of Viṣṇu, I spoke.

p. 198) Wherever the performance of Vedic rites has indeed ceased, there let the Tantra be set in motion. Those Brahmins who have been consumed by curses and are deprived of the Śabdabrahman [should be engaged]. || 209 ||

This is indeed their family dharma, the means for attaining both worldly enjoyment and liberation. Those Brahmins born in the sacred seats (pīṭha), whose brahminhood has been consumed by a curse, [follow this path]. || 210 ||
In their lineage, this entitlement to this path arises;
because it is honored within that very lineage, it is called the Kaulīna path. || 211 ||
Therefore, those who belong to the Kṣatriya and Vaiśya castes follow an inferior path compared to them; it is declared that their entitlement there is as sacrificers.
The Siddhāntin is inferior to that [Kaula], and therein lies the eligibility of the Śūdra. Those who enter the Kaula Dharma without knowing the lineage [of transmission]—|| 213 ||
They will be destitute, lacking progeny, and afflicted by disease; of this there is no doubt. For he who is unaccomplished in the Kaula knowledge yet desires to eat meat [is lost]. || 214 ||
O Goddess, he is a perpetrator of great sins, excluded from all rites—a wicked soul who has abandoned the conduct of the observance and follows his own whimsical impulses. || 215 ||

Successes do not come to one whose family perishes; therefore, one should not associate with such a person. He who, casting aside the injunctions of the scriptures, conducts himself according to his own whims, [attains neither success nor a noble lineage]. (216)
He does not attain success in this world, nor does he reach the supreme goal in the next; he becomes an object of reproach in the world and likewise in the Veda. || 217 ||
Relying on the non-visualization of the source (yoni), one should partake of the family substances (kuladravya).
He is born among the sources of beings (bhūtayoni) numbered by the hairs on his body. || 218 ||
If one whose mind is intoxicated by liquor perceives nothing at all, there is for him no meditation, no practice of austerity, no dharma, and no virtuous action. (219)
If there is no divine power, no guru, and no self-reflection in the Kaulika path, one who is merely attached to sense-objects will surely fall; of this there is no doubt.
One who knows the distinctions of the three genders and discerns the six supports (ādhāras), having arrived at the sacred seats (pīṭhas),
should take refuge in the great sacrificial forest.
Having gone again and again from the mūlādhāra up to the aperture of Brahmā (brahmarandhra),...
By means of the Ciccandra-kuṇḍalinī-śakti-mudrā, one shall possess a disposition of bliss.
One should become devoted to drinking the nectar flowing from the lotus of the sky; this is declared to be the drinking of honey, while others are merely drinkers of liquor. || 223 ||
Having severed both merit and demerit with the sword of knowledge, the knower of yoga should always dissolve the mind into the Supreme; he is called a "consumer" (palāśī). || 224 ||
Having restrained the collection of one's own senses with the mind, one should unite them within the Self; such a person is said to be a "fish-eater," while all others are of the nature of fishermen.
That power which is unawakened becomes awakened for the Kaulika;
he who serves that power shall be a true servant of power. || 226 ||
Thus, I have declared the secret reality of the five mudrās; having understood this correctly from the mouth of the Guru, he who practices them shall be liberated. (227)
Now, the manner of worship, which is difficult for you to obtain, shall be described.
One should effect the purification of the deity through substances that are not present within the self. || 228 ||

Bathing, the twilight rites (*saṃdhyā*), purification of the elements (*bhūtaśuddhi*), breath control (*prāṇāyāma*), and stabilization; through the placement of the *mātṛkā* and other such practices, there shall be the purification of the self. (229)
By means of sweeping, smearing with cow dung, and other such acts, it has been made like the surface of a mirror.
This purification of the site is considered to be accomplished by means of canopies, incense, lamps, and so forth. || 230 ||
Having interwoven the syllables of the root mantra with the letters of the Mātṛkā.
This purification of the mantra is considered to consist of three repetitions, both in direct and reverse order. || 231 ||
Having consecrated the articles of worship with the root-mantra and the weapon-mantra, the one who knows the ritual procedure [should proceed].
And one should display the dhenu-mudrā; this is considered the purification of the substances. || 232 ||
Having established the deity upon the pedestal and performed the ritual of sakalīkaraṇa, one should sprinkle it with the water of the arghya offering while reciting the root mantra;
then, one should present the offering of a lamp. || 233 ||
Having thus performed the purification for the deity, one should thereafter perform the sacrifice;
that worship should be known as fruit-bearing, otherwise it would be fruitless. || 234 ||
Worship without a mandala is proclaimed to be fruitless; therefore, having drawn it according to the rules with mantras, one should perform worship therein. || 235 ||
That which, having an unbroken circular form, stands pervading the universe and adorns the three worlds—that mandala is Sadāśiva. || 236 ||
The garden of Kāmarūpa is square, while that of Jālandhara is circular;
Pūrṇagiri is considered to be full, like a half-moon. (237)
Having worshipped the mandala, one should subsequently place the support in the proper sequence.
The conch, the vessel for the *arghya* offering, and the five vessels for enjoyments, worship, and the *bali* offering. || 238 ||

Having established [the vessel] from one's own right to the left and having worshipped it with wine purified by mantra, O Mistress of the Kula, the knower of the ritual procedure should fill it completely.
In that [vessel], one should place liquor and meat in the measure of a *māṣa* bean;
[these should be] those that are spoiled, stale, leftover, foul-smelling, or devoid of fragrance. (240)
Satisfying [the ancestors] with offerings placed in another's vessel by means of such causes would be fruitless.
And with most delicious substances, overflowing with intoxication, resembling nectar. || 241 ||
And the gratification of the goddesses with captivating [offerings] shall become fruitful. Unconsecrated liquor is sinful and bestows quarrels, disease, and suffering. || 242 ||
It destroys longevity, prosperity, fame, fortune, dharma, and learning; therefore, having consecrated the family substance according to the rules, one should then worship it. || 243 ||
Well-prepared liquor removes disease, suffering, and calamity.
It increases longevity, prosperity, fame, good fortune, dharma, and knowledge. || 244 ||

Otherwise, without consecrating the substances, the donor and the consumer go to hell; of this there is no doubt. Without the perfuming of the substances, one should neither recollect nor chant. (245)
Those great fools who merely remember [the mantra] suffer misery at every step. Without the destructive [power], there is no mantra; without the mantra, there is no destruction. (246)
Through purification by means of gazing, touching, meditating, mantras, and mudrās, the substance becomes fit for libation and brings delight to the deity. || 247 ||

(200) One should invoke the ninety-four *kalās* produced from the syllables of fire, sun, moon, and the *praṇava*. [The mantra for worship is: *oṃ hrīṃ namo 'gnisūryacandrarūpavarṇapraṇavodbhavābhyaś caturṇavatikālābhyaḥ svāhā*. Having thus invoked the ninety-four *kalās* by number...
One should worship. || 248 ||
There, while meditating upon one's chosen deity, one should thoroughly investigate the meaning of the verse.
One should recite these verses afterwards; listen, O beloved, as I speak them. (249)
Place [my mind] in that Supreme Nectar-Self, which produces unbroken, singular-flavored bliss, whose form is the spontaneous vibration of consciousness, and whose nature is immortality. || 250 ||

O Supreme One, who resides in the non-clan (akula), whose form is nectar, and who brings about the knowledge of purity—bestow the state of immortality upon this substance which has a moist form. || 251 ||
Having performed the touch of the hand upon that which possesses such a form, O you whose nature is the elements!
Having become the supreme form of immortality within me, manifest your radiance! || 252 ||
Oṃ [Oṃ Klīṃ Hrauṃ Jūṃ Saḥ, O Immortal One, O Source of Nectar,

O Mistress of Nectar, O Showerer of Nectar, cause nectar to flow, cause nectar to flow, Svāhā! Having uttered "Klīṃ Hrauṃ Jūṃ Sa," [one says] "O Immortal One, O Source of Nectar, O Mistress of Nectar."
One should utter the word "amṛtavarṣiṇī" (the showerer of nectar). || 253 ||
"Amṛtaṃ srāvaya yugaṃ svāhā" is the mantra for the purification of substances; it is proclaimed as the Amṛteśī-mantra consisting of thirty-five syllables. || 254 ||
Having invoked three times as previously described, [one should do so] three times with the *dīpanī* mantra.
Having touched the vessel of worship, one should honor it with the dhenu-mudrā.
This life-force, which contains the essence of all the remaining scriptures originating from the fragments of the cosmic egg,
brings forth the nectar-like flavor of the great intoxicant.
Even with that pure substance, and even with perfumes, flowers, and unbroken grains of rice.
And likewise, one should bathe oneself with all the mantras prescribed for the ritual placement (nyāsa).

One should offer libations to the lineage of the venerable gurus at the crown of the head and to the sandals at the *mūlādhāra*. First, one should satisfy the Divine Current (*divyaugha*): Ādinātha, who is Sadāśiva; || 258 ||
Īśvara, Rudra, Viṣṇu, and Brahmā together with their wives—these become twelve; thereafter, one should offer libations to the hosts of Siddhas. || 259 ||
The four beginning with Sanaka, Sujāta adorned with beautiful ornaments, Sanatkumāra, Vyāsa, Vāmadeva, and likewise Śuka. || 260 ||
Dattātreya and Raivataka [protected] exactly twelve Manus.
One should satisfy Nṛsiṃha, Maheśa, and likewise Bhāskara.
One should employ the names Mahendra, Mādhava, and Viṣṇu at the end; likewise, Mahāśiva in the lineage of the Siddhas (Siddhaugha) and Sadāśiva in the lineage of humans (Mānavaugha). || 262 ||
Then one should perform the worship of the supreme, divine, and auspicious seat;
thereafter, one should invoke the Goddess with two mantras and likewise worship her.
O Mother, O Supreme Goddess, who dwells within the Great Lotus Grove, whose form is the bliss of the primal cause, and who is devoted to the welfare of all beings, come here today! 264.
O Goddess of gods, easily accessible through devotion, adorned with all ornaments:
remain perfectly steady here while I worship you. || 265 ||
Having meditated, one should then display the mudrās and offer perfumes, flowers, unbroken grains (akṣata), and so forth.
Of that which consists of consciousness, which is immeasurable, devoid of qualities, and bodiless.
The conceptualization of the form of Brahmā is for the benefit of practitioners.
In the liṅga, on the sacrificial ground, in fire, in water, on a wooden plank, on the head, and in a mandala. || 267 ||
Worship is proclaimed to be of ten kinds: in an image, on a wall, and in the heart. People devoted to the ritualistic section (Karmakāṇḍa) represent the formless as having form. || 268 ||
Just as milk produced from all the limbs of a cow flows forth from the openings of her udders, so too does the omnipresent Lord manifest within images and other such forms. 269.
Due to its primordial nature, because it is the first of all things, and especially because of the worship and the faith of the practitioner, the deity attains presence. || 270 ||
Residing within the entire body of cows, it does not nourish itself; yet that clarified butter (ājya), fashioned by good karma, would nourish even that [body] in return. || 271 ||
Thus, the Supreme Lord resides within every body like clarified butter;
yet without worship, the God does not bestow fruit upon men. || 272 ||
Having unified his vital breaths and his sense faculties, he [should meditate].
O Goddess, one should worship [the deity] after having installed it; otherwise, it is considered fruitless. || 273 ||

Whatever may be deficient in mantra, deficient in ritual action, or deficient in the yantra—just as a missing limb [renders a body incomplete], [the syllables] Laṃ and Kṣaṃ accomplish everything. || 274 ||
O Daughter of Śambhu, for those who do not understand the pervasion of the *yantra* of the Lord in the form of the mantra, all worship and other rites performed become fruitless. (275)
In the left [tradition], it is at Kauleyantra-pīṭha and in the place of the image (mūrtisthāna); in the right [tradition], it is at Vaidika;
but in the Svayambhū [tradition], it is self-arisen, worshipped, and bestows happiness. || 276 ||
Since the Veda is beginningless and self-existent, the deity resides therein.
Because it is accessible and subject to destruction, such Tantric worship is of that nature.
Because it restrains all suffering arising from defects such as desire and anger.
They call this a *yantra*, for within it the deity is fully worshipped.

The yantra should be drawn in a clockwise direction for worship in the Dakṣiṇa tradition; it is drawn in a counter-clockwise manner in the Kaula and other traditions. This [method] has been revealed as a secret. || 279 ||

One should worship [the deity] along with the limbs and the enclosures using the sixteen services; for all the days, one should perform the great sixteen-fold rite with perfumes, flowers, unbroken grains, and so forth.

One should worship each [deity] by their respective name, preceded by the syllable *praṇava* (oṃ) and ending with *namaḥ*. Then, according to the path taught in the Āgamas, one should offer libations (*tarpaṇa*) with drops of curd. || 281 ||
Lifting it silently with the nails of the thumb and ring finger, one should draw it out.
For one who is unworthy, this [offering] consists of eight [units], and he should satisfy the face of the deity.
Having offered the single libation and having recited the root mantra and the pādukā-mantra, [one should proceed].
Having recollected the internal power, one should satiate the deity of the body.
The thumb is the station of Bhairava, while the ring finger belongs to Caṇḍikā.
Therefore, that machine which is to be propitiated by those two is indeed dear to them.
And for the rite of subjugation (vaśyakarma), one should offer libations using the thumb and middle finger.
In rites of sorcery, one should offer libations by joining the index finger and the thumb.
In the rite of immobilization (stambhana), one should offer libations by joining the little finger with the thumb.
Having thus offered libations to the deities and others, one should worship the lineage of gurus. (286)
If [one meditates on her] holding a mudrā and a human skull filled with honey in her two hands,
resembling molten gold, and adorned with red flowers, ointments, and garments;
With a focused mind, he worships the lineage of gurus, who are endowed with sidhdas, whose side-glances are full of compassion, whose eyes are reddish, and whose hair is like the color of the sky.
Having thus performed worship with incense, a lamp, and even an offering of food, |||
In this manner, one should likewise offer fruits such as plantains, as well as betel leaf.

One must certainly perform the worship of Baṭuka at the beginning, at the start of the left [path], and so forth; in this path, Baṭuka is the principal deity, fashioned by the end of the liquor (surā) and other elements. || 289 ||
Therefore, one should not perform that worship of the deity without him; for he who worships Mahādeva without first honoring the Baṭuka [is guilty]. (290)
There is no fruit from worshipping him alone, and Baṭuka becomes enraged;
therefore, one should worship him along with his retinue using perfumes, flowers, wine, and meat. || 291 ||

Through the ritual application of their respective mantras, the deity shall attain satisfaction. Then one should offer a bali-oblation to the Lord of the Field (Kṣetrapati); hear his mantra. || 292 ||
The two *tāras* [Oṃ Oṃ]: “Oṃ Oṃ! O Devīputra Baṭukanātha, resplendent with a mass of tawny matted hair, tawny, three-eyed, with a face of blazing fire! Accept, accept this offering of worship!
Hūṃ Phaṭ Svāhā! Then, having spoken “Devīputra,” he says “Baṭuka” and “Nātha.”
Resplendent with a mass of matted hair, tawny like that of a Kapila bull.
One should recite this offering mantra for the three-eyed one with a face of fire-flames: "Gṛhṇa-gṛhṇa hūṃ phaṭ svāhā. It consists of forty-six syllables. || 294 ||
Having thus recited the mantra, one should then recite this verse: "May Baṭuka, who grants all accomplishments, be satisfied by the offering of the bali. || 295 ||

May he, who is attended by bhūtas and vetālas, grant me constant peace. [Oṃ Oṃ Oṃ, homage to all yoginīs, all ḍākinīs, all śākinīs, and those dwelling in the three worlds; [accept] this offering of worship and bali.]
"Grasp! Hūṃ Phaṭ Svāhā!"—one should utter all the preceding mantras in their proper sequence. || 296 ||
"O Yoginī, Ḍākinī, Śākinī, dweller in the three worlds! Homage to you! Please accept this offering of worship. || 297 ||
Having likewise uttered "huṃ phaṭ," one should then speak the word "svāhā" at the end.
This mantra is proclaimed to consist of forty-four syllables. || 298 ||
Whatever yoginī there may be—whether fierce, gentle, most terrible, or supreme; whether moving in the sky, on the earth, or in the ether—may she be ever pleased with me. (299)

One should utter the three *tāras* [Oṃ Oṃ Oṃ], then say "to all beings" (*sarvabhūtebhyaḥ*) and "to all" (*sarvam eva ca*). Afterwards, "to the lords of all beings" (*bhūtapatibhyaḥ*) ending with the heart-mantra (*hṛdanta*) constitutes the seventeen-syllable mantra. (300)
Those beings of various forms who dwell in the heavens, on earth, and in the atmosphere;
And those dwelling in the depths of Pātāla were purified by the yoga of Śiva.

May Dhruva and the others, those of true resolve, as well as Indra and the others who are established [in their stations], be satisfied with joyful minds; may these beings accept this bali offering. (302)
The three *tāras* [Oṃ Oṃ Oṃ]: "Come, come, O son of the Goddess, Baṭukanātha, taker of leftovers!
Haṃ Hūṃ Haṃ Hūṃ Haṃ Hūṃ Haṃ Hūṃ! O Protector of the Field, destroy, destroy all obstacles along with all ritual offerings; this..."

"Accept, accept the offering of worship, *huṃ phaṭ svāhā*! Likewise, come, come, O son of the Goddess, young boy, now! Then one should utter "haṃ hūṃ haṃ hūṃ" twice for the remover of leftovers (*ucchiṣṭahāriṇe*). || 303 ||
"Kṣetrapāla! Śarva! Destroy the obstacles—this pair."
One should recite this mantra for the offering-bali, accompanied by all ritual services. || 304 ||
*gṛhṇa gṛhṇa hūṃ phaṭ svāhā*—this is the mantra of sixty-four syllables.
This is declared to be the mantra of Kṣetrapāla, which bestows all supernatural accomplishments (siddhis). || 305 ||
I dwell in this field as a servant of that guardian of the field (Kṣetrapāla). May he, being pleased by this offering of oblation, grant me protection from all dangers. || 306 ||

Oṃkāratritayaṃ [oṃ oṃ oṃ huṃ śrīṃ hsauḥ hrīṃ hrīṃ huṃ huṃ, for the accomplishment of the mantra from the heart of Akṣobhyānanda presided over by Bhairava, descend, descend! To the Kṣetrapāla, the Great Kṣetrapāla, vāṣaiṭra huṃ |] huṃ śrīṃ.
One should then utter "hūsauṃ ca hrīṃ hrīṃ. Then, at the end of the pair of "huṃ"s, one should say "akṣo" for the one presided over by Bhairava. || 307 ||
From the heart of supreme bliss, for the sake of mantra-siddhi, he uttered the two syllables: "Kṣetrapāla mahākṣetrapālāya vauṣaṭ hūm. || 308 ||
This mantra, consisting of forty-nine syllables, is remembered as the supreme one that brings great delight to the most excellent Kṣetrapāla. || 309 ||
Afterwards, one should utter the three *tāra*s (oṃ āḥ hūṃ) and say: "O Rājarājeśvara, for such-and-such Kṣetrapāla, this worship and offering [is made]; hereafter... (310)
This mantra, ending with two *ṭha*s and preceded by *gṛhṇa*, is said to bestow all desired things even in times of adversity.
In the worship of the deity known as Rājarājeśvara.
By this offering of the bali-oblation, may the Lord, the King of the Kings of Kings, together with his host of young attendants, be forever gracious unto me. || 312 ||
One should offer the *bali* to the *baṭuka* in the west, the *yoginī-bali* in the north, the *bhūta-bali* in the east, and the *kṣetrapāla-bali* in the south. (313)
Having worshipped the Lord of the Kings of Kings in the center, one should offer the bali.
The bali offering for Baṭuka should be made with the thumb and the ring finger. || 314 ||
The offering to the Yoginīs should be made with the index, middle, ring, and thumb fingers.
And with all his fingers, the twice-born man should offer the bali-oblation to the spirits.
The offering to the Kṣetrapāla should be made with the thumb and forefinger.
And for the Lord of the Kings of Kings, [it is performed] with the thumb and the middle finger. || 316 ||
Having thus worshipped the Baṭukas and others, one should display the Kula-lamps; a devotee of the Deity should fashion them from fine flour to a height of four finger-breadths. || 317 ||
[He saw] very beautiful triangles, shaped like lamps and hand-drums.
One should have nine, seven, or five [vessels] made that hold one karṣa of clarified butter.
Having unified the inner light and the outer light into those of immeasurable radiance, one should offer the family-lamp (kuladīpa) by waving it three times above the Goddess. || 319 ||
O Goddess, Navātmikā, who are joined with the Mistress of the Wheel (Cakreśī) and all the wheels, accept this *ārātrika* for my spiritual accomplishment. (320)
Having then displayed the lamps of the lineage, one should perform the worship of Śakti.
Delighting in the dust of the guru’s feet, he is endowed with faith and devotion. || 321 ||

"Having caused one's own power (sva-śakti), the hero’s power (vīra-śakti), and the initiated [consort] who embodies the Guru to drink [the wine], one should then drink it oneself; such is the certainty of the scripture. || 322 ||
But he who consumes the family substance (kuladravya) without first offering it to Śakti—his worship is fruitless, and the deity is not pleased. || 323 ||
