The Cāṇḍālī, the Carmakārī, the Mātaṅgī, and likewise the Pulkasī; the Svapacī, the Khaṭakī, the Kaivartī, and the Viśvayonikā. || 324 ||
This is declared to be the group of eight families (kulāṣṭaka); now the group of eight beyond family (akulāṣṭaka) is described: Kuḍukī, Sautrikī, Śastrījīvā, and Rañjakī. || 325 ||

The female singer, the washerwoman, the artisan, the woman of the Kauśika clan, and likewise the eighth; these women, endowed with the mantras and observers of the rules of conduct, [should be honored]. || 326 ||
One should immediately perform the consecration with the respective mantras individually.
One who stands on the path of the Kula should perform worship there, while recollecting the Śakti.

Whether she be a maiden, one established in a vow, or even one who bears the yoga-mudrā—if she arrives spontaneously at the time of worship, she should be immediately worshipped by the wise. || 328 ||
In the absence of a woman of the aforementioned caste, one should worship a woman from any of the four castes who is beautiful, youthful, peaceful, compliant, joyful, and pure. (329)
Free from disease and endowed with devotion, she subsists by following the teachings of the wise; she is free from greed, virtuous, smiling-faced, and speaks kindly. || 330 ||
Devoted to her guru and the deity, she is pure-minded and dear to the Kaulikas; she is free from malice, possesses specialized knowledge, and is eager in the worship of the deity. || 331 ||
Foul-smelling, miserable, foolish, aged, insane, a betrayer of secrets, prone to fallacious reasoning, contemptible, stubborn, shameless, and fond of quarreling. || 332 ||
A woman who is deformed, walking on a wrong path, wicked, lame, blind, or having a distorted face—a yogi should indeed avoid such a woman, even if she is joined with mantras. || 333 ||
Then, preceded by the mantra and water, the practitioner of mantras should offer all [the rites] beginning with worship to the Goddess, starting from the east, using this mantra. || 334 ||
The remaining rites, such as the disposal of the leftovers and so forth, should be performed as in the case of the *dakṣiṇā* offering.
Then, the remainder may be given at will; that is said to be for the *śeṣikā*. (335)
"Eṃ hṛducchiṣṭacāṇḍālini [Eṃ namaḥ ucchiṣṭacāṇḍālini mātaṅgi sarvavaśaṅkari svāhā. This is the mantra. One should utter the word 'mātaṅgi';
then 'sarvavaśaṅkari svāhā' consists of twenty-one syllables. (336)
With this mantra, one should offer the remains of the floral offerings (nirmālya) to Śeṣikā.
One should meditate upon the goddess Ucchiṣṭamātaṅgī, who alone deludes the world.

Delighting in the entertainment of lute-playing and song, radiant in her blue silken garment, with lips like the *bimba* fruit and feet richly stained with fresh lac, her garment reaching to her ears;
lovely-limbed, wearing white conch-shell earrings and resplendent with rubies as ornaments—(p. 205).

I bow down to Mātaṅgī, the goddess with a beautifully smiling face, dark as a parrot. Then, having lifted the vessel with both hands, one should offer it, together with its companion, to the one who is the form of the venerable Guru and is directly Paraśiva himself.
One should worship together with heroes who are well-connected to the authentic tradition; having marked one another, one should drink [the substance] with their permission. || 340 ||
Having lifted the vessel with the left hand and formed the mudrā with the right, one should take it with the second [hand] according to the rule while reciting the mantra. || 341 ||
"I drink this purifying nectar, the medicine for existence; it is the cause proclaimed by Bhairava for the total eradication of the drinking of intoxicants. (342)
Because it has the independence of wealth as its essence, because it consists of bliss, and because all states of being are composed of that [bliss],
those states are submerged within the aesthetic flavor (rasa).
To expand one's own sovereignty, wine is drunk;
therefore, with all my desires fulfilled, I drink this Goddess who is wine. (344)
O gods, the knower of mantras, with a mind undisturbed, should slowly partake of the honey-drink while reciting this root mantra.
A piece of meat the size of a bean and wine the measure of a handful should first be accepted by the Guru;
he shall then be the giver of the remainder to the disciples. || 346 ||
Having taken the liquor given by the Guru along with its accompaniment, one should drink it.
And having sat down in the presence of women, gurus, elders, and those worthy of honor. || 347 ||
One should never drink liquor, nor likewise drink it without a mantra; he who drinks liquor without a mantra is declared a drinker of *surā*. (348)
Situated within the triangle that is one's own self, possessing a radiance equal to ten million suns.
One should offer the substance accompanied by the mantra into the form of consciousness shaped like a coiled serpent (kuṇḍalī). || 349 ||
This supreme nectar, filling infinite vessels, has the characteristic of being both an oblation and an acceptance within the fire that consists of the supreme I-consciousness. || 350 ||
One should indeed contemplate with the intellect the identity of the Guru, the deity, and the mantra.
One should drink the honey through instructions until the point of complete exhilaration.
Poison at the end of a meal, and food at the end of drinking liquor—know that to be nectar, which one should drink together with this [liquor]. || 352 ||
Wine accompanied by the act of chewing (carvaṇa) is always said to be nectar;
drinking it without chewing is merely the consumption of poison. || 353 ||

Drink is said to be of three kinds, according to the divine (divya), heroic (vīra), and animal (paśu) sequences: the divine drink is that which is drunk in the presence of the Goddess; the heroic is that which is prepared on a soft seat. || 354 ||
Having drunk like an animal according to one's own will, as proclaimed by Paśupati, you shall now declare the Kaulika conduct which bestows the fruits of both worlds. || 355 ||

The ritual of the "union of vessels" (pātramelāpaka), which brings about friendship, is now proclaimed. Neither father nor friend is its protector; it is encompassed by the union of worthy recipients. || 356 ||

One should never perform the union of vessels (*pātramelana*) with those who are uninitiated, who lack proper conduct, who are ignorant of the mantras, who disregard the deities, who corrupt the covenant (*samaya*), who have strayed, and who follow the path of worldly proliferation (*prapañca*)— even if they possess the splendor of Brahman. [Rather, it should be performed] with those who are devoted to your worship.
[They are] peaceful, with their backs turned toward the wealth of others. || 358 ||
They were skilled in family traditions, promoters of the ancestral path, beloved by women, praised by women, fortunate, handsome, and speakers of gentle words. || 359 ||
And by those who are well-versed in the family path, well-guarded, learned, and handsome.
By those who have achieved their practice, who are rich in wealth, fortunate, and full of desire; || 360 ||
When those liberated by Brahman and honored by kings meet through the turn of fate, they should effect a union with a worthy recipient;
thus, the increase of happiness shall belong to both. || 361 ||
One should not use a single vessel unless it is the Lord of the Family himself; otherwise, the mantras turn away and obstacles arise at every step. 362.
One should not give even to Bhairava one's own vessel that serves as the basis for one's livelihood;
if one should give it out of delusion, one would incur the curse of the deity.
The seat, the food, the bowl, and other things such as the bed;
One should never cause confusion with those who lack direct knowledge and those who are unworthy.
Or, according to the division of the tradition (mnāya), one may perform the "merging of vessels" with the Kaulikas; [the word *ālopa* is an archaic form].
There is a union of the east and south, and likewise of the north and west.
The full vessel (pūrṇapātra) offered by the male and female practitioners (yogis and yoginīs).
Then, one should drink [the water] over which the root-mantra of the *samantrapāduka* has been recited. || 366 ||
If, by chance, one obtains a vessel of liquor, one should take it with devotion, recite the mantra as before, drink it, and remember the Guru. || 367 ||
And for those endowed with the power of the Guru, as well as for the elder and younger disciples of the Guru.
One may eat the leavings even of one's own elder brother, but never those of anyone else.
The elder should join with the younger, but he should not cause him to grasp it again thereafter.
One should drink wine that is the remnant of Śakti, but chew the food that is the remnant of Vīra.

One should not give what is left over from one's own meal, nor should one eat what belongs to another. One may eat the leavings of women, but one should not give one’s own leavings to women. One may eat the leavings of women, but one should not offer one’s own leavings to them. (370)
One should also establish the maṇḍala there for one's own gathering; then one should worship the vessel, honor the Goddess, and perform the libations and other rites. || 371 ||

Having raised them, one should place each other's vessels into one another's hands; one should meditate on the unity of the two as being mutually one—this is the "Merging of Vessels" (pātramelana). || 372 ||
I shall now proclaim the worship of the wheel, which is concealed within all tantras.
There exists nothing else superior to this for bestowing the attainment of one's desired goals. || 373 ||

She is beloved by all the gods and is said to bestow whatever is desired; she should be propitiated even by those following the Vedas for the sake of accomplishing their goals, as was done by the ancient priest (purohita).
O Goddess, having performed the Kaulika rite, their heart's desires shall be fulfilled.
Lakṣmī, having slain the demon Kolāsura, drank his blood entirely. (375)
Then, intoxicated by drink, she was laughed at at will by the Brahmins—even by Brahmā, Viṣṇu, or even by me—who desired to question her. (376)
Then the Buddha, the Great Lakṣmī, vanished from the earth; everything became bereft of splendor and appeared as if it were about to die. || 377 ||
Dharma does not waver anywhere, nor do the deities feel satisfied; thus, when a hundred years had passed, they went to Brahmā for refuge. || 378 ||
Even Brahmā appeared there devoid of splendor, looking like a pauper. The sages then asked, "O Creator, from where has this loss of splendor come? (379)
Then, O beloved, the laughter that had been provoked was explained by Brahmā: "This is the great splendor of Brahmā; Viṣṇu has merely remained silent. (380)
Because she was laughed at by Śiva due to the obstruction of your side, she became angry;
therefore, she departed for the netherworld (rasātala). || 381 ||
Consequently, all the brahmins in the world were bereft of fortune and became destitute.
Therefore, Viṣṇu, Śiva, and I, as well as you all led by Śakra, [are one]. || 382 ||
And the Nāgas, the Pitṛs, the Siddhas, the guardians of the quarters, the Yakṣas, and the Rākṣasas.
Let them propitiate that goddess and praise her with great hymns.
Then they all gathered together and went to Mount Śrīśaila.
Having seen some splendor of Śrī, they then performed her propitiation.
They praised him with various hymns through Vedic and Tantric paths;
thus, after three years had passed, Śrī became manifest before their eyes. (385)
And beholding him with a compassionate gaze, he spoke these words with a smile: "For what reason were the brahmins made to laugh, and why are the gods agitated? (386)
Furthermore, for what reason was worship offered to her who is difficult to behold?
Then she was addressed by me: "The entire universe is pervaded by you. || 387 ||
"They do not know your power and mock you because of your actions; having understood this, O witness of my heart, I laughed. (388)
"Your power, however, is unknown to all the brahmins, gods, and asuras. Therefore, O Lord, be gracious and carry out the course of the world. (389)
Having heard these words spoken by me, Śrī indeed said: "This liquor is my sister; therefore, its worship is the foremost. (390)
"Whosoever shall perform [this] for the God, that God will rejoice;
just as this expansion of illusion becomes useless without me. || 391 ||
Furthermore, all such worship is in vain without the worship of the Cakra, whether one desires worldly enjoyments in this life or divinity in the next. (392)
At that time, the worship of the wheel with mantras must indeed be performed as required; it is dear to all the gods and must be kept secret. Now, I shall explain its ritual procedure.
That worship of the entire wheel is proclaimed to be eightfold; it is performed when a task has arisen by the thousands, or when a task has reached completion. || 394 ||
On the day of the festival for the deity, or even upon the arrival of a Kaulika; during the Umāmāheśvara yoga, or during the yoga of the union with Śakti. (395)

In the kingdom of Bali, on the day of Kāma, the worship of the discus (Cakra) bestows great joy; it may be performed at dusk, at the Abhijit muhūrta, or at midnight, when conjoined with the eighth lunar day.
If on the ninth day there occurs the yoga named Umāmāheśvara, and on the eighth or fourteenth day of Mars (Tuesday), this is the Śaktisaṅgama yoga. || 397 ||
During the dark fortnight of the month of Āśvina, for five days beginning with the thirteenth, this reign of King Bali is proclaimed for the purpose of sporting according to one's desire. || 398 ||
They say that day is "Kāmadina" when the thirteenth lunar day falls on a Monday; having bathed on the preceding day and worshipped the Goddess with one's desired object [in mind], || 399 ||
Having performed [the preliminary rites], one should resolve upon the worship of the wheel and offer the *bali* sacrifice to the animal;
I shall now fully explain that procedure, and one should also arrange for the secondary alternative (*anukalpa*).
Bali is said to be of three kinds: Tāntrika, Smārta, and Vaidika.
Among these, first of all, the Tāntrika is recorded as being of eight types.
The human, the buffalo, the boar, the goat, the sheep, the crane, the pigeon, and the cock—these are the general [animals], each succeeding one being inferior to the preceding. || 402 ||
In that Kali age, O Goddess, at this great sacred seat (mahāpīṭha), a man who is a hero (bali) is the most excellent;
he should be employed by the lord of practitioners, for he attains beauty immediately. || 403 ||
One who is bound by the elements, has black eyebrows, lacks fields and such, and is born in the inverse order [of castes].
Whether acquired for a price, or desired, or arrived spontaneously by fate. || 404 ||

Whether for a year or for six months, one who has maintained his conduct according to his desire shall be fit for the bali offering; no other [meat], such as that taken by thieves and the like, is suitable. || 405 ||
The Mahiṣa [wind], born of the forest, is five yojanas above and ten below;
it is extremely cruel and is entirely black in color. || 406 ||
With slightly reddened eyes, upward-pointing horns, a long tail, and well-fleshed body; being of a single color, possessing the hue and form of the deity, and free from disease. || 407 ||
He should be a bull with testicles, possessing horns, the leader of the herd, and endowed with fragrance through medicinal herbs and other substances.
Having rendered it odorless, this most excellent [substance] is fit for offering to Bala. || 408 ||
For all castes as well as for the deities alike, this sacrifice is distinguished by its entitlement and its capacity to bestow delight. || 409 ||
A ram with horns is preferred, though in some cases even one without horns is acceptable; however, one that is maimed, lacks testicles, or is too young or too old, is not recommended. (410)
And having been reared at home for more than two years, he has become exceedingly strong.
Indeed, the excellent crane is truly equal to this [man] in terms of his burden of flesh. || 411 ||
The pigeon has a throat with the hue of a blue-necked peacock and possesses full shoulders.
One that has been nourished at home for more than a year is said to be suitable for the purpose of the *bali* offering.
He who, possessing many colors, cries out at dawn before all others.
But one that is fleshy, of a single color, or with copper-colored crests, is especially distinguished. || 413 ||
A man must not be killed by the twice-born, nor a buffalo by a Brahmin; chickens have been brought to equality with pigs by all those who offer oblations. (414)
The kūṣmāṇḍa, the coconut, the bilva fruit, and likewise the sugarcane;
Having wrapped it in cloth, one should cut it with a knife or similar instruments. || 415 ||
This is declared by those who follow the Dharmaśāstras to be the bali offering pertaining to the Smṛti.
And it has been stated that even in each preceding case, the one who pleases the deity is distinguished [as superior]. || 416 ||
The deity is pleased by whichever form one has greater devotion toward; thus, endowed with all the observances (niyamas) and restraints (yamas), one should worship the embodiment of the Self.
One should offer the Vedic bali-oblation consisting of cooked rice mixed with boiled mung beans.
Along with Rocanā, it is for the very fierce deity, accompanied by Vaṭakas. || 418 ||

Having worshipped Bali according to the rules with perfumes, flowers, unbroken grains (akṣata), and so forth, one should utter the syllable Om (tāra), the Kali-yuga mantra, "O Mistress of Sacrifice" (yajñeśvari), and the word "Loha. || 419 ||
"Daṇḍāyai namaḥ"—this mantra consists of sixteen syllables.
Having recited [the mantra] one hundred and eight times, the practitioner should then rise.

Having meditated upon the sacrificial animal (paśu) as having the form of the Goddess, one should cast upon it a flower consecrated with the root mantra, along with unbroken rice grains (akṣata) and sandalwood paste. || 421 ||
When he, having been seized, moves his body by his own will, as long as the victim does not move his body, he is not killed. || 422 ||
Having turned facing north and likewise looking at the *bali* offering which faces east, the practitioner should thereafter utter this mantra: || 423 ||
"You, an animal, have appeared before me by virtue of my good fortune in the form of Bali; therefore, I bow to you who possess all forms in the form of Bali. (424)
Through the gift that pleases Caṇḍikā, the donor’s misfortunes are destroyed.
O Bali, for the sake of the sacrificial offering to Cāmuṇḍā, salutations be unto you! || 425 ||
"Animals were created by the Self-Existent One himself for the sake of sacrifice; therefore, I cause you to be slain today, for in sacrifice, O kinsman, there is no killing. (425)
With the mantra "Oṃ Śrīṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ," [offer] the bali, which is my own form.
Having reflected thus, one should place a flower upon his head with the *mūlamantra*.
And you are the worshipper of Caṇḍikā, the adorer of the world of the gods; with the mantra "hrīṃ hrīṃ khaḍga," one should fully worship that sword. || 428 ||
Reciting the mantra "māṃ hrūṃ phaṭ," one should cut the sacrificial offering (bali) with a single blow;
thus severed, it brings satisfaction to the deity. 429.
If a sound is made when a blow has fallen, it is not done in an emergency.
Within a year, the destruction of the kingdom will certainly occur. || 430 ||
Having thus properly offered the bali-oblation and performed the ritual of purification (tyikarma), women and men should invite [the guests] during the third watch of the day. || 431 ||
For the pleasure of this goddess and for the fulfillment of my heart's desire.
Indeed, you have been invited by me tomorrow for the festival of the Cakra-pūjā.
Eight women should be invited, but fewer may be invited for my sake. Men should be fewer than the women; if there are more men, they bring about loss. (433)

Those established in all the Kaula observances, even if they are devoid of the Eastern and Southern traditions, become intent upon initiation and are to be invited for the worship of the Cakra. || 434 ||

On that night, having personally worshipped the deity without weariness, one should recite the mantra "Kula-śabda" (specifically *kulakulakulaje piśācini svāhā*) twice; then, at night, one should mutter one thousand and eight times the thirteen-syllable mantra ending in *svāhā*, beginning with *kulajā piśācinī*. Thus, one should recite it during the night.
One may likewise see an obstacle to the wheel or that which is auspicious. || 436 ||
When an obstacle is perceived, one should not perform the rite, or else it should be preceded by a propitiatory ceremony (śānti).
The pacification rite for Gaṇeśvara, the fire-oblation for the planets, and that for Bhairava; || 437 ||

Then, one should offer the outer *bali* and recite this mantra: Oṃ [oṃ oṃ oṃ] namaḥ amuka-kṣetrapālaka ehyehi bhagavan pūjāṃ gṛhṇagṛhṇa baliṃ bhakṣabhakṣa cakravighnakarān stambhayastambhaya huṃ phaṭ svāhā.
Having uttered "Namas" three times, [address him as]: "O Kṣetrapālaka named so-and-so! (438)

Come, come, O Blessed One; accept this worship, as well as the pair of offerings and the pair of oblations. Devour the pair, and paralyze the pair of those who create obstacles to the wheel. || 439 ||
The mantra consisting of seven and four syllables, "huṃ phaṭ svāhā," is thus proclaimed. Having completed the duties of the day, one should worship the Cakra in the evening. || 440 ||
One should place the vessel filled with wine within that circle of one's own vidyā;
having invoked the Goddess there, one should perform the worship. || 441 ||
One should provide various kinds of meats, many species of fish, and four types of edible foods, accompanied by side dishes. || 442 ||
Having properly worshipped the Goddess, together with her limbs and her retinue, the wise ones—
And likewise, the Śaktis and the Vīras should be worshipped with flowers, unbroken rice grains (akṣata), and other offerings. || 443 ||
Within the interior of the house of worship, inside a triangular earthen chamber, one should worship Ucchiṣṭabhairava with intense perfumes, flowers, and other offerings. || 444 ||
There will be the fault of impurity from food remnants during the great festival of the Cakra-pūjā.
In order to avoid those faults, I worship Bhairava.
Three *tāra*s (oṃ), likewise two for Ucchiṣṭabhairava, then "gṛhṇa" twice, followed by *huṃ phaṭ svāhā*—this is the twenty-two-syllable mantra. || 336 ||
With this, one should perform the offering of the bali at the conclusion of the worship;
having returned to the hall of worship, one should prostrate before those seated in the maṇḍala. || 447 ||
The Guru, taking the vessel filled with the nectar of wine in his hand, [should proceed].
One should sprinkle [the assembly] with water and recite the hymn for the pacification of misfortune. || 448 ||
The goddesses chant the praise of Hara’s lotus feet, which bestow grace, the nectar of liberation, and the gift of immortality.
I bow to the host of yoginīs who possess perfect contentment and who awaken the intellect to the infinite Siddhānta.
I bow my head to the Lord Bhairava, the beloved of Bhairavī, who stands in the center of the circle of Yoginīs and is surrounded by the mandala of the Mothers. 450.
Salutations to the venerable Lord-Physician, who destroys the darkness of beginningless and terrible saṃsāra, and who provides the medicinal remedy for the kula. 451.
May all calamities, misfortunes, and diseases resulting from the transgression of conventional conduct perish through union with the Divine Wheel. 452.
Longevity, health, sovereignty, fame, gain, auspiciousness, and victory.
May there be beauty and the fulfillment of desires; may all the deities protect [you]. || 453 ||
Of those who worship, those who protect, and of the masters of self-restraint, the lords of yoga, and those whose wealth is asceticism.
May the Blessed One, the Lord of the Family, bring peace to the entire kingdom and to the sovereign of others. || 454 ||

May the families of practitioners rejoice, as well as those people who are spectators of this creation, and those who belong to the great lineages spoken of by the Guru. May all those devoted to the Kula and Kaula traditions rejoice, as well as others who are supreme, and those Śāmbhavas who distinguish the various special stages. 455.

May the Siddha-gurus and the successive lineages following them rejoice; may the elders, the juniors, the initiates, the young students, and the maidens rejoice. Born within the noble family of heroes and the six Yoginīs, may the lords of the earth, cattle, the twice-born, and the virtuous people rejoice.

May those who are skilled in ethics, established in faultlessness, free from envy, incomparable, and free from affliction, rejoice— those teachers who are eternally devoted to the stainless, profoundly peaceful, whose minds have reached the end of all qualities, and for whom fear and sorrow have been removed.

May those devoted to yoga rejoice, as well as those joined to the Kula-yoga, and the teachers, initiates, practitioners, and spiritual sons. May the cows, the twice-born, young women, ascetics, and maidens rejoice—those who are intent on meditative cultivation and endowed with devotion to the Guru. 458.

May the lineages of practitioners rejoice, established in powers such as *aṇimā*; may the curses of the Yoginīs fall upon the enemy at the appointed time. May that indescribable state of Śambhu’s grace manifest, in which only the lotus-feet of the Guru are to be found. (459)

Those abodes which exist in the sequence of the wheels (*cakra*), those which are situated within the channels (*nāḍī*), those which dwell in the pores of the skin— the trees of desire— and those which are established within the elements (*dhātu*).
May those goddesses, who dwell upon the waves of the ocean of exhalations and whose abode is inhalation, intent on devouring the faction of enemies and worshipped by the Kaulas, be satisfied. 460.

Those goddesses who have arisen from the Kula, those deities dwelling on the earth, those of eternally celebrated splendor dwelling in fire, those Mothers who abide in their own source; those consisting of the nectar of the sphere of immortality in the sky, and those who are all-pervading at all times— all of them [are present].
May those devoted to preserving the family path grant me peace. || 461 ||
Whether situated above in the Egg of Brahmā or in a city, in the expanse of the sky, on the surface of the earth, in the partless realm,
in the netherworld, in fire, or in water and wind— wherever that may be;
or having set foot in sacred fields, seats, secondary seats, and so forth.
May the goddesses, who are always pleased by offerings of incense, lamps, and the like, and who are worshipped by the lords of heroes, protect us once they have received the ritual oblations. 462.

Brahmaśrī, Śeṣa, Durgā, Guha, the Baṭukas, the Gaṇas, the Bhairavas, the Kṣetrapālas, the Vetālas, Ādityas, Rudras, the Planets (Grahas), Vasus, Sages (Munis), Siddhis, the Guhyakas and others; the Bhūtas, Gandharvas,
Vidyādharas, Ṛṣis, Pitṛs, Kiṃnaras, Yakṣas, and Nāgas.
May all the lords of yogis, the cāraṇas and others, the sages, and the gods who dwell within the discus protect [us].

May all the deities residing within the body, the elephant-faced ones, the lords of the sacred fields (kṣetrapālas), the Bhairavas, the Yoginīs, the Baṭukas, the Yakṣas, the Pitṛs, the Bhūtas, the Piśācas, and the Grahas; as well as others who move on the earth, in the cardinal directions, or through the sky— the Vetālas and the Ceṭakas— be satisfied.
"Drink my excellent beverage, O noble son! || 464 ||

If the gurus, gods, and ancestors are indeed true, if the Vedas and Āgamas are true, if the Yoginīs are pleased, if the Supreme Deity exists, and if the Vedas are indeed authoritative; [then this is so].
If the Śākta system is shown to be authoritative, and if the Kaulika system is likewise true, then may I always be victorious. || 465 ||
May all the practitioners, the oceans, and the lords of the hosts be satisfied; may the Yoginīs and the Kṣetrapālas who are established within my body [be satisfied]. || 466 ||
From Śiva down to Anila, and including all beings from Brahmā down to a blade of grass.
"Let all beings, from Kālājña up to Śiva, be satisfied by this sacrifice of drink. || 467 ||
Then, having lifted up that vessel and performed the ritual dismissal (samudvāsya), the Guru should give what is contained in the jar to the disciple and separately to each of the Yoginīs. || 468 ||
In the same manner, he should drink from the vessel himself for the heroes and for others as well.
One place is for women, and another distinct place is for men.
Alternatively, having formed pairs, one should seat them in order, either in the form of a row or again in the form of a circle. || 470 ||

One should worship all [the goddesses] within the center of the wheel with the thought that they are Śiva and Śakti. In that state, regarding the mantras and the heroes (vīras), there is no distinction between what should be done and what should not be done. || 471 ||
In that regard, whatever action is performed, whether auspicious or inauspicious, all of it arises for the pleasure of the deity; there is no doubt in this matter. (472)

Idle chatter is said to be the fruit of recitation; drowsiness is designated as meditative absorption (samādhi). Physical transformation is declared to be worship; that which is vomited is the offering (bali) to Bhairava. || 473 ||
Liberation would be the union with power; praise is speaking at that time.
The placement [of mantras], the touching of the limbs, the act of eating, and the performance of the oblation; || 474 ||
Meditation (dhyāna) is said to be gazing, while lying down (śayana) becomes sandalwood (candana).
And whatever activity is performed by those who have brought about that manifestation is itself a true ritual act.
He who deliberates upon what ought and ought not to be done is a sinner; O Goddess, those who have entered this wheel are to be known as supreme yogis. 476.
By means of which human beings attain the very form of Gaurī herself—joy, the pacification of anger, as well as falling [down] and singing. (477)
The playing of flutes, lutes, and other instruments; the composition of poetry and the like; weeping and speaking; as well as rising up and yawning. (478)
O Goddess, movement is a modification; this is designated as yoga. When, having abandoned the modification of the mind, the outpouring [of consciousness] proceeds, [that is yoga]. (479)
At that time, however, the foremost of yogis attain the state of divinity.
The fool-minded person who reviles the Kaulikas, who are possessed by Bhairava, [is lost]. || 480 ||
The yoginīs destroy that without a doubt; there is no uncertainty in this matter.
Whatever wonder arises among the Kaula people through the immersion of devotion, [that is the true Kaula]. (481)
That very thing will undoubtedly come to pass, whether it be auspicious or inauspicious.
O Goddess, for your mind is always attached to the deity and you are indeed pure.
*Tāra*, *namas* to the Blessed Lady who dwells upon wine and meat! O Goddess of the Wheel, beloved of those who follow the *Kaula* path, speak! || 483 ||
Having said, "May the truth residing in my mind be realized," one should offer liquor mixed with meat to the Kaulikas;
they then recite those mantras for him.

In that regard, if someone is not a Kaula, that Speech does not manifest for him. One should not revile, laugh at, or become angry with those who are intoxicated by the honey [of the wine] within the Cakra. 485.
One should not disclose news concerning this circle to outsiders; one should not harbor malice toward them, nor should one act in a harmful way. 486.
One should indeed protect her who is to be protected and guard her with great effort;
seeing those agitated by passion within the circle, one should contemplate them with the thought that they are deities. || 487 ||
One should neither criticize nor laugh; through devotion, he shall go to the state of the Yoginī. When the wheel of Bhairavī is set in motion, all castes become twice-born. 488.
When the Bhairavī-cakra has ceased, all the castes become distinct once again. Such is the majesty of the cakra through its application in the worship of the Goddess. 489.
Whether it be a woman, a man, a eunuch, an outcaste, or even a most excellent twice-born;
Within the center of the wheel there is no division; all are remembered as equal to the gods.
All men situated within the center of the wheel are of the nature of Śiva; all women are Pārvatīs. Therefore, one should not create any distinction between them. || 491 ||
Even with thousands of jars of wine and hundreds of loads of meat, Mahāmāyā is not satisfied without the nectar of the bhaga and liṅga. || 492 ||
A lustful man should not approach a woman who is unwilling or uninitiated;
however, he may approach a woman who has been purified by the immediate consecration, since she is prescribed [for such union]. || 493 ||
From the worship of a thousand wheels, a king who has fallen from his kingdom shall regain it; with fifty, one obtains a son; and with ten, one becomes free from disease. (494)
He whose devotion to the worship of this wheel falters due to some obstacle from yoga will inevitably become a sovereign emperor within the course of a year. || 495 ||

One should perform worship in five ways for the sake of attaining desired beloveds; with seven [ways], there shall be the attainment of wealth—this is the ritual procedure for the worship of the Cakra.

He who gives his sister, daughter, or wife to a practitioner of the lineage (kulayogin)—whether he be intoxicated by honey-wine or whether he be without a wheel (acakre)—is indeed a partaker of merit. (497)
The daily worship is said to be the best; the worship on festival days is middling; the monthly worship is declared to be the lowest;
but after a month has passed, it becomes fruitless.

Whether in a month, an intercalary month, six months, or even a year, one should worship the venerable Guru with devotion; likewise, when they are present, one should worship his wife, sons, and so forth. In their absence, one should worship a member of his family, a disciple, or another yogi.
One should satisfy [the deity] with substances equal in weight to oneself, preceded by the worship of the Cakra. || 499 ||
In the face of diseases, calamities, faults, evil associations, and ill omens;
O Goddess, one should worship the assembly of Yoginīs for the pacification of that fault.
"You shall describe the procedure for the Navarātra, which bestows all desired objects. On the first day (pratipad) of the bright fortnight of Āśvina, [one should perform] the one-year rite. (501)

For those two years old, [the rite is performed] on the second day; in this manner, one should increase it further for the subsequent ages. On the ninth day, she is nine years old, beautiful, and free from physical defects.
Śuddhā, Bālā, Lalitā, Mālinī, Vasundharā, Sarasvatī, Ramā, Gaurī, and Durgā are proclaimed as the nine. || 503 ||
Having completed the worship of the deity with devotion after being invited in the morning, [one should proceed].
Having purified her with an oil massage and a bath, one should lead her to the place of worship. || 504 ||
Having seated the young girl in the presence of the deity, one should worship her.
With perfumes, flowers, unbroken grains of rice, incense, lamps, and the illuminators of the lineage. || 505 ||
With various kinds of foods to be chewed and swallowed, with drinks, and with milk, clarified butter, honey, and meat;
One should satisfy her with fruits such as plantains and coconuts. || 506 ||
O Goddess, being himself endowed with power and filled with the radiance of youth, he should recite his own mantra according to his capacity, increasing it by one [repetition] at a time. || 507 ||
Afterwards, one should contemplate one's own chosen deity (iṣṭadevatā) adorned with a young girl;
then, having paid homage to her with the thought that she is the deity itself, one should dismiss her. || 508 ||

One should worship them individually with their respective names preceded by the three *tāra*s (oṃ āḥ hūṃ), ending with *namaḥ*, followed by the word for the deity, and suffixed with the dative case. || 509 ||
One should worship the five-year-old boy (Baṭuka) and the nine-year-old Lord of the Gaṇas (Gaṇeśvara) with perfumes and other offerings, both at the end and at the beginning in due order.

Then one should offer the worship performed during the Navarātra to the Goddess; having given betel-leaf and a sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā), one should bid farewell to that young girl (kumārī). || 511 ||
He who thus performs the worship of nine young maidens every year shall be happy in this world,
and upon death, he shall become a god.
Alternatively, the knower of mantras should worship with devotion nine beautiful young women who have reached the prime of youth, as the nine Mothers. || 513 ||
Hṛllekhā, Maṅganā, Raktā, Mahocchuṣmā, and Karālikā—[these are the goddesses].
[He worships] Durgā, who is the action of will and knowledge, as well as Baṭuka and Gaṇeśvara.
Having worshipped as before, one should satisfy [the deity] with substances such as wine and the like.
With his self enriched by all sovereign powers, he shall become dear to us both. || 515 ||
On a Friday during the Vārendra yoga, [one should approach] a beloved woman who has ascended the prime of youth.
Endowed with all auspicious marks, agreeable, and captivating to the mind.
Or likewise, having invited and summoned a woman from a noble family who is in her menses;
One should have her, whose limbs are purified by an oil massage and a bath, sit upon a seat.

Having adorned [the deity] according to the prescribed rite with perfumes, flowers, and ornaments, the practitioner should likewise adorn himself with perfumes, flowers, and other such items. || 518 ||
Having invoked the deity into that [liṅga], one should worship it according to the sequence of months,
performing the ritual service, offering incense, and lamps that illuminate the lineage.
Having presented [the offerings] with the perception that they are deities, using articles endowed with the six flavors.
One should gratify [the deity] with great devotion by means of meat and other foods, both solid and soft.
One should visualize [the deity] as being endowed with mature exultation and recite the mantra.
Possessing the full bloom of youth, he himself became entirely intent upon that meditation.
Having offered the recitation and other rites one thousand and eight times with an unwavering mind,
he should then spend the night together with her.
Having performed this on Saturdays, one is liberated from the property of a Brahmin;
indeed, poverty shall be destroyed after five Saturdays.
And his lineage remains unbroken, with prosperity secured by seven Bhṛgus.
By performing [this] on nine Sundays, one shall attain union with the deity.
"You shall declare that the worship of the couple is the means for accomplishing all desires; one should perform it during a solar transit, at the equinox, or during the solstice. (525)
Gaurī and Śiva, Ramā and Viṣṇu, Vāṇī and the Lotus-seated One (Brahmā), Śacī and Indra, Rohiṇī and the Moon, and likewise Svāhā and Agni. || 526 ||
Having worshipped the nine couples—Bhadrakālī and Vīrabhadra, as well as Bhairavī and Bhairava—by means of the very same path previously described. || 527 ||

One who knows the ritual procedure should [worship] with the respective names, preceded by three *tārās* (the syllable *oṃ*) and ending with *namaḥ*: [oṃ oṃ oṃ gaurīyai namaḥ; oṃ oṃ oṃ śivāya namaḥ; oṃ oṃ oṃ ramāyai namaḥ; oṃ oṃ oṃ viṣṇave namaḥ; oṃ oṃ oṃ vāṇyai namaḥ; oṃ oṃ oṃ brahmaṇe namaḥ].
Having worshipped with perfumes, flowers, and other offerings, one should satisfy [the deity] with wine and other such substances.
One should also cause the couples to perform movements endowed with the radiance of the mature finale; when this is done, there is no doubt that the nine deities will be satisfied. || 529 ||
He who performs this every year shall not encounter suffering; for the sake of a son, one should do it nine times, and for the sake of wealth, every month. (530)
On the Ayana and Viṣuva days, for the sake of release from prison, or for the sake of virility for a eunuch,
one should perform this eight times.
Now, that deity of the Kaulika paths shall also be described: through her, sins are destroyed and happiness arises; she is worshipped on the lunar days (pakṣas) within those years.

On the first day of the bright fortnight of Māgha, having abstained from food during the day, and having bathed and put on white garments, he should perform the evening twilight devotions (sāyaṃsandhyā). || 533 ||

Performing the worship of the Sun according to the prescribed method and provided with all necessary materials, one should recite the mantra with undistracted mind until the setting of the moon. (534)
In this manner, one should worship every day on the fourteenth day of the bright fortnight; on the full moon day, one should worship the Śaktis and Kaulikas according to one's ability.
One should meditate upon the deity situated in the moon, accompanied by the radiance of youth. Having performed the white worship in this manner, one is liberated from the sins of the night. (536)
Just as one performs worship during the bright fortnight, so too during the other fortnight;
he who acts according to the prescribed rule attains all desires. (537)

Then, on the first day of the bright fortnight of the month of Vaiśākha, the Goddess, having risen during the Brāhma-muhūrta and performed her bath and the twilight devotions (sandhyā), [proceeded]. || 538 ||
Standing in a pleasing and secluded place, facing the eastern direction, and having adorned oneself with perfumes, flowers, and other offerings, one should proceed. || 539 ||
At the first twilight, when the solar disc has not yet risen, one should meditate upon the chosen deity together with its retinue and worship it with all the ritual offerings.
Then, having performed the worship of the wheel (cakrapūjā), one should display the family lamps (kuladīpa) and offer edible items such as fish and meat to Śiva in the form of the Guru.

Having offered that to the Goddess, he himself, endowed with faith, should drink the remainder according to his capacity, accompanied by the joy of youth and with a mind free from conceptual constructs. || 542 ||
One should meditate upon that Goddess within the mandala, reciting the mantra one thousand and eight times; having offered that worship, one should dismiss the deities. (543)
Thus, beginning from the first day of the bright fortnight, one should perform recitation and worship day by day,
remaining steadfast until the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight.
On the day of the new moon (amāvāsyā), the triads and other odd-numbered Kaulikas are to be worshipped.
When they have become united as a pair, it then dispels the sin committed during that year. || 545 ||

Having thus worshipped at the time of midday, the powerful one, by worshipping again in the evening, his fame spreads to the ends of the quarters. (The word "his" is to be supplied as the subject. 546.
For one who worships during the two twilights, prosperity faces every direction.
The Yoginīs become submissive to him who worships them at the three junctions of the day.
Free from greed for wealth, one should worship the fifty pairs beginning with Śrīkaṇṭha according to the procedure previously described. || 548 ||
One should cause couples here to engage in the play of mature passion;
they grant the desired fruit to the practitioner who is satisfied. || 549 ||
Keśava and the others, Gaṇeśa and the others, Kāma and the others, as well as the Pīṭhas and so forth.
Having worshipped [the deity] like Śrīkaṇṭha and others, one is glorified in that respective world.
The earth, the ground, the directions, the waters, the mountains, the sky, and all moving beings;
There are a thousand times ten million yoginīs, and there are as many bhairavas as well.
All of these have indeed been appointed for the protection of the family; on special days, they shall all be of joyful mind. (552)
They do not afflict practitioners at all out of a desire for their own worship; for when unworshipped they create obstacles, but when worshipped they become gracious.
They protect those who are devoted to their gurus, those of virtuous conduct, and those who guard the Dharma.
They destroy those illuminators who are devoid of devotion and of evil conduct.

Now I shall declare the determination of the meaning of the scriptures concerning the path of the Kula tradition: if the eldest son born into a Kaula family has not been initiated, [the lineage is not established]. (555)
If the youngest member has been initiated, he should perform the family worship;
at the conclusion of the worship, having taken the remains, he should offer them to the eldest.

It is the settled rule that the youngest should take his leftovers. Furthermore, if the Guru, an elder, or one worthy of worship should arrive during the course of the worship, [one should act accordingly]. || 557 ||

Having bowed, one should state one's intent; the rest should be performed with his permission. One should perform the daily worship (nityārcana) by day and the occasional worship (naimittikārcana) at night. || 558 ||

When many have gathered together at the prescribed time for the worship performed for specific desires, they should bow to their respective gurus and satisfy [the deity] with mantras according to their own respective traditions. || 559 ||
One should not perform the Kula worship without the ritual destruction [of impurities], without bathing, without scents, flowers, and unbroken grains (akṣata), and without liquor and meat. || 560 ||
One should not perform worship while talking idly, nor without the mantra; likewise, one should not drink without the ritual vessel (śakti), nor should one offer worship with only one hand. 561.
One should not drink with a single hand, nor should one discharge spittle within the circle (cakra). One should enter the circle after bowing down, and likewise depart from it after bowing down.
One should not sit upon the Śrīcakra, nor ever upon the vīrāsana.
One should not construct a Śrīcakra on one side, nor should one worship in a single vessel. || 563 ||
The vision of the Śrīcakra removes the sins from the eyes of men; if that were not so, the pair of eyes belonging to a Kaulika would be nothing but a pair of sores. || 564 ||
Those of improper conduct and those of proper conduct, those established in the Wheel, and the Śakti-kaulikās.
One should contemplate all beings with the thought that they are Śiva and Gaurī; one should not treat them with contempt.
Having gone to the house of the family preceptor, one should with devotion request nectar-like food for the purification of sins;
in its absence, one should drink water. || 566 ||
If a worthy recipient is given [the gift] with devotion by the family preceptor according to his capacity, one should receive it after paying obeisance;
otherwise, one shall go to hell. (567)

One who wears a turban, one wearing a bodice, one who is naked, one with disheveled hair, one who has already eaten, one who has not bathed, one who is not very hungry, and one who is turned away during a dispute [should not be questioned]. || 568 ||

This does not apply to one born in such a family, nor to a twice-born man who is refined; yet even one who studies the Vedas may become destitute through the consumption of the family’s wealth. || 569 ||
By spitting the nectar of yoga and by circumambulating a vessel of liquor, [one attains the goal].
By drinking [the water] with the neck held upwards, one incurs the curse of the deity. || 570 ||
Those who sit upon a single seat, those who eat from a single vessel, and those who drink from a single bowl—these certainly go to hell. || 571 ||
Those who serve the family property while the Guru resides in a single village, as well as those born in that family, his son, his own elder brother, or the family preceptor; || 572 ||
Without permission, that evil-minded person shall go to the Raurava hell. One who is impure from eating should not touch the Cakra, the family substances, or the Guru. || 573 ||
Having washed the family vessels with water on the outside, one should cause them to be offered;
however, having removed a vessel that held liquor, one should not worship it.

One should never cast a drinking vessel or a jar of liquor into the center of the circle; rather, with a pure mind, one should perform the washing of hands, mouth, and so forth within the circle. || 575 ||
The fool who performs these acts becomes a vessel for calamities:
spitting, excrement, urine, and the discharge of downward wind. (576)

He who performs [this] in the center of the Śrīcakra becomes a beast for the Yoginīs. Likewise, if the vessel in the center of the cakra is broken, or if the offering-bowl is spilled, [the same occurs]. || 577 ||

If the lamp is extinguished, there will be suffering for the kingdom; therefore, one should perform the worship of the wheel. One should avoid joking, idle chatter, mockery, and excessive speech. (578)
One should avoid indifference, fear, and anger in the center of the wheel.
One who holds a vessel in his hand should not bow while in the midst of the circle, nor should he offer a full vessel [of water].
One should not hold the bowl in the hand for a long time, nor should one touch it while holding other vessels in the hands; one should not touch the bowl with the feet, nor should one ever break it.
One should not give with only one hand, nor should one let a drop fall to the ground. One should not move the vessel from its place, nor should one drink without employing the mudrā. 581.
Even while speaking, one should not drink liquor, nor should one cause a mixing of vessels.
Two parts of the vessel are filled with wine, while the third part is empty.

One should not strike one bowl against another, nor should one strike a bowl against the ground. One should not lift a bowl that has no supporting base, nor should one set it down on a surface that lacks support.
One should not leave a vessel empty, nor should one step over it. Having washed the vessel with cow dung, one should look upon a Brahmin at the end of the *namaḥ* mantra. 584.
The exposition of the Dharmaśāstra, associating with women of noble family, and fellowship with those learned in the Vedas (śrotriya) constitute the performance of Vedic rites. || 585 ||
It destroys desire, wealth, life-span, fame, gain, knowledge, happiness, and so forth; therefore, one traveling on the Kaula path should never perform [such acts]. 586.
He who gives the *kuladravya* belonging to the Śrīcakra to one who is not of the *akula* lineage should be known as a great sinner;
he shall go to the Raurava hell. || 587 ||
One should not engage in verbal dispute even with an enemy while in the midst of the assembly; one should regard him as equal to a father or mother and endure the harsh words he may utter.
Having bowed with devotion and preceded by the word "Śrī," the wise man should proclaim the names of the Śrīguru, the Kula scriptures, and whatever other objects of worship there may be. (589)
Furthermore, by adhering to the tradition, all practices such as the recitation of mantras and so forth, when obtained from the mouth of the Guru, become fruitful; it is not otherwise.
One should worship the Śrīśāstra daily and must not place it in the house of a paśu.
A practitioner of Tantra should employ the ritual instruments (kalaśa-āstras) as if they were his own wife.

One should avoid all treatises on animal sacrifice as one would avoid another's wife; likewise, one should avoid Vedic texts that are corrupted by ritual refinements, broken, or have their syllables disordered. (592)
One should recite the mantras according to the tradition; by means of them, there shall be stability in this matter.
But that conduct which is contrary to the Dharmaśāstras is indeed Kaulika. || 593 ||
One should not cause these to be made into wheels; one should worship them as goddesses. One must never step over them;
having done so, one would fall into hell. || 594 ||
A mother, the wife of a guru, a sister, a sister’s daughter, a brother’s wife,
the wife of a hero, a maiden, and one observing a vow— 595.
One with missing limbs, one with deformed limbs, one who is agitated, one who is pleased, and one who is composed.
He approached his daughter-in-law once out of desire; she was old and not at all beautiful.
One should worship Manoharā, a Kaulika woman who is in the prime of youth, well-attired, possessing a beautiful smile, with dark limbs and eyes whose corners are red. || 597 ||

One should not, out of sudden impulse or by force, approach a Kulayoginī; rather, one should unite with her when she is herself agitated within the circle or when she herself makes the request. || 598 ||
Raw meat, a jar of liquor, a rutting elephant, and the sight of a perfected being (siddha).
And young maidens, eager for play, [climbed] the mango trees and the *aśoka* trees. || 599 ||
Upon seeing a solitary tree, a cremation ground, a gathering of women, or a woman dressed in red garments, one should pay homage with devotion. (600)
The Guru, the Śakti, the son, the elder, the younger, and the lineage-teachers.
The scriptures of the Kula tradition, the Kula substances, and the Kaulikas.
As well as those who incite, those who indicate, those who speak, and those who show.
[He saw] teachers, enlighteners, yogins, yoginīs, and perfected beings (siddhapuruṣas).
One should not revile, loathe, laugh at, or insult a maiden, a young girl, a naked woman, nor even a madwoman. || 603 ||
One should not speak what is unpleasant or untrue to any true yogi of noble lineage.
One should not say of a woman of good family that she is "ugly" or "excessively dark-complexioned. (604)
One should not examine the deeds or omissions of devoted heroes;
nor should one look at a woman who is fallen, naked, insane, or with her breasts exposed.
One should not consort with a woman during the day, nor should one gaze at her private parts. Even if a woman has committed a hundred offenses, one should not strike her even with a flower. || 606 ||
One should not enumerate the faults of women, but should rather manifest their virtues alone;
for the yoginīs of noble lineage always abide within the trees of the family.
One should not eat from its leaves, especially from those of the *arka* tree; one should not sleep beneath a family tree, nor should one cause any harm. (608)
Having seen [it], one should pay homage with devotion; one should never cut it down.
Śleṣmāntaka, karañja, akṣa, nimba, aśvattha, and kadambaka; || 609 ||
The bilva, the vaṭa, the udumbara, and the ciñcā—these are recorded as the ten [trees]. The penance prescribed by Bhṛgu consists of renunciation and the observance of vows. || 610 ||
A follower of the Kaula path, however, should avoid going on pilgrimages and the like.
He who treats with contempt a guru who has bestowed upon him even a single syllable; || 611 ||

Having passed through a hundred births as a dog, he shall attain the state of a caṇḍāla. If by the killing of one there is security for many, and a virtuous destiny [for the many], [then it is permissible]. 612.
Internally Kaula, externally Śaiva, and among the people Vaiṣṇava— one should conceal the Kaula,
O Goddess, like the water within a coconut fruit.
The wise one should reveal the Guru, but he should guard the mantra with great effort.
Through both non-illumination and illumination, wealth and life-span are diminished. || 614 ||
One who has fallen away from all proper conduct should take refuge in the conduct of his family.
One who has fallen away from the conduct of his family shall go to the Raurava hell. || 615 ||
A true guru should not speak of the Vāmācāra to one who is not of noble lineage;
if the disciple falls from right conduct, that guru becomes a sinner. || 616 ||
If some beloved person of a Kaulika is beset by great calamity, one should perform the worship of sixty-four deities for the sake of removing his suffering. || 617 ||
On one day, or eight days, or sixteen days;
or for thirty-two days, or sixty-four days, it should be performed according to its gravity.
One should have it made or perform it oneself, avoiding any stinginess regarding wealth; having fasted there, with a purified soul, one should perform the nyāsas previously described. || 619 ||
While the world of living beings was fast asleep, he, joyful in soul and high-minded, [beheld] Brāhmī, Māheśvarī, Kaumārī, and likewise Vaiṣṇavī. || 620 ||
Vārāhī, Indrāṇī, Cāmuṇḍā, Mahatī, and Ramā—these indeed have been declared by me to you as the eight Mothers (Aṣṭamātṛs). || 621 ||
Asitāṅga, Guru, Caṇḍa, Krodha, Unmattakapālin, Bhīṣaṇa, and Saṃhāra—these eight are considered to be the Bhairavas. || 622 ||
Having sipped water (ācamana), one should worship them with the supreme [mantras] in the Mithuneṣṭi sacrifice, as before.
The task will undoubtedly be accomplished, reaching up to the limit of the intense expansion at the end.

If performed for the propitiation of the deity, the preliminary practice (puraścaryā) is distinguished; yet for one devoid of devotion to the guru, austerity, knowledge, vows, and lineage [are of no avail]. (624)
All [ornaments] are as useless for a corpse as various types of jewelry and decorations; therefore, the guru should always be served through the actions of mind, speech, and body. (625)
One who perceives the teacher as a mere human, the mantra as a collection of syllables,
and the images as mere stone shall go to hell.
This path of the family tradition has been fully revealed by the Guru. || 626 ||
If it is practiced correctly, it is the means for both enjoyment and liberation.
Even a Brahmin, though endowed with virtues, is not praised if he is not devoted; even a Mleccha, though devoid of virtues, is called a disciple if he possesses devotion.
Indeed, one should perform what is beneficial for the guru through the actions of speech, mind, and body.
Due to practicing what is harmful, a disciple is born as a worm in excrement. || 629 ||
From abandoning the guru comes death; from abandoning the mantra comes poverty.
By abandoning the guru and the mantra, one shall go to the Raurava hell.
One should contemplate in one's heart the words spoken by the guru, the Supreme Person, and his blessings.
Even when struck by others, one should remember with serene faith: "This is [the grace of the Lord]. || 631 ||
One should offer all objects of enjoyment and consumption to the Guru; considering them as his remnants, one should joyfully accept them by his command. || 632 ||

One should not engage in the non-payment of debts, nor in the giving away or the buying and selling of goods, together with those who are not one's gurus; nor should one marry a woman born of such a family.
One should not reveal the secret meaning spoken in brief to just anyone; if one were to speak it, they would undoubtedly fall from both [attainments]. 634.
Even if a disciple were to give away his entire possessions to the guru while being devoid of devotion, he does not obtain the fruit; for devotion alone is the cause. || 635 ||
Whatever substance the Guru has a desire for, he should not experience it himself; or, if it must necessarily be experienced, he should do so only by his command.
For he who takes even a very small amount of a teacher's property that was not given to him, having entered the womb of an animal, is devoured by carnivorous beasts. (637)
Disobedience of commands, embezzlement of wealth, and acting contrary to the wishes of the guru—these they call "offense against the guru";
he who commits such an act is indeed a sinner.
One should not treat one's teacher, friends, companions, servants, female slaves, and others with contempt. || 638 ||

One should not revile other traditions, such as the Vedas, the Shastras, or the Agamas; nor should one desire various enjoyments consisting of sandals, seats, clothing, vehicles, fly-whisks, and the like. Upon seeing the Guru, one should offer salutation and not long for worldly pleasures. 639.
Whatever the Guru may say, whether it be right or wrong, one should perform it without hesitation; for in both restraint and favor, the Guru is the cause of everything.
Whatever has issued from the mouth of the Guru is called the entire scripture. When capable of performing the Guru's work himself, he should never send another.
One who is exceedingly devoted should perform many services for others, even when accompanied by them.
Whether standing, waking, sleeping, eating, or drinking, one should contemplate the Guru.
One should carry out only the command of the guru with an inner self absorbed in him; one must not harbor pride on account of caste, learning, wealth, and so forth. || 643 ||
One incurs that very sin by speaking untruth in the presence of a guru.
The sin that one would not incur by killing a cow or a Brāhmaṇa— || 644 ||
The lion-throne should be given to the Guru; the highest seat to the elders; the seat of the rite (vidhyāsana) to the juniors; and for others, an ordinary seat. (645)
Or one who is distinguished by birth, learning, or wealth, having seen the Guru from afar, [should approach] with joy.
Having performed a single prostration like a staff, one should perform three circumambulations.

But when there is a conjunction of gurus with a guru, one should first salute one's own guru; then one should salute that [other] guru, and thereafter the disciple should cause [the musical instruments] to be played. || 647 ||
One should perform three prostrations to the guru and one single prostration to the elders.
In the same way, one should offer a salutation with joined palms to those worthy of worship, and a physical prostration to others.
One should honor the gods, teachers, family preceptors, elders, the aged, and those whose wealth is asceticism.
One should always bow down to those learned in the Vedas who are superior in knowledge and established in their own duties.
One who is cursed by women, one cursed by a preceptor, a heretic, an outcast, and a rogue.
One should not bow down to one who performs forbidden acts, one who is ungrateful, or one who does not abide by the stages of life (āśrama).
He who, residing in the same village, eats after having offered [food] to his guru, by him that which is eaten becomes impure; he is born as a pig after death. || 651 ||
A disciple residing in the same village should pay homage to the guru at the three junctions of the day.
Standing even at a distance of one krośa, one should bow to the guru every day with devotion.
A disciple should prostrate at the five joints [of the body] from a distance of half a yojana;
starting from one yojana up to a limit of twelve yojanas.
A disciple staying in a distant land has, through devotion, come into his presence.
One should prostrate to the Guru during the months numbered according to those respective yojanas.
When the disciple is situated at a great distance, he should go [to visit] whenever he so desires; however, he must not see a king, a deity, or his guru with empty hands.
One should offer fruits, flowers, garments, wealth, and other such things according to one's ability. The Brahmin who does not worship in this manner shall become a Brahma-rākṣasa. || 656 ||
The Guru’s wife, his sons, and the Guru’s eldest brother are equal to the Guru himself; he protects his younger brothers like himself and his sons. (657)
One who does not disclose one's own knowledge, religious observances, asceticism, or dharma.
And he is the illuminator of the castes, the stages of life, knowledge, austerity, and dharma.
He who is well-versed in the six rites, who is a giver and an enjoyer rather than a beggar—he alone is a Kaulika Ācārya; any other is a mere mockery of the Kula.
He who correctly understands the Piṇḍa, the Pada, the Rūpa, the Rūpātīta, and the Nirañjana—he is the Guru and shall uplift others. || 660 ||
O Dear One, he who understands the threefold nature of the tethering post, the Vedic initiation, and the seizing of the sacrificial animal— he is declared to be a Guru.
O lady of excellent hips, he who knows the rules for the secret meaning of the Paśus, Pāśas, and Paśupatis is proclaimed as a Guru. (662)
Compassion, doubt, fear, shame, and disgust as the fifth; lineage, conduct, and likewise power—these eight are proclaimed to be the fetters (pāśas). (663)
One bound by fetters is called a beast (paśu), while one freed from fetters is Maheśvara.
Therefore, he who removes the fetters here is called a Guru, and no other. (664)
He who [resides] upon the seven lotus petals from the root-center up to the aperture of Brahmā (brahmarandhra).
O beloved, he who knows the living, moving fruit is the Guru; no other.
For a disciple who is terrified by the fear of saṃsāra, the guru [should act] with reverence.
One who destroys fear through vows, fasts, and observances is considered a Guru. || 666 ||
Indeed, that guru who bestows his own spiritual power upon his disciple in an instant— being himself devoid of any beginning in ritual action— is difficult to find in the Kali age.
A wise man should choose that very guru from whose contact supreme bliss arises, and no other. || 668 ||
The entire three worlds, including all moving and non-moving beings, were begged from him out of fear; he by whom that very fear was consumed is a Guru difficult to find on earth. (669)
And just as a honey-seeking bee goes from flower to another flower, so should one proceed.
Likewise, a disciple who is greedy for knowledge may go to another teacher from his own guru.
Even though he is detached, the Guru, by the command of Śiva, for the sake of the disciple’s qualification, should wait for some time and only afterwards hand [the disciple] over to another.
One should never break the uninterrupted Kaula tradition; as long as the tradition exists, so long shall the state of the Yoginī endure. (672)
If both the teacher and the disciple, out of delusion, give or receive instruction without examining one another, they shall both attain the state of a piśāca.
But he who imparts instruction without performing the consecration is of deluded intellect; his mantra surely perishes, like a grain of rice sown in sand. || 674 ||
If one should initiate an unworthy person out of desire for wealth, fear, greed, or similar motives, [the teacher incurs a fault].
One incurs the curse of the deities, and what has been performed becomes fruitless.
Having worshipped the Kula-cakra according to the prescribed rite with the substances of the Kula, one should properly show it to the disciple; this is considered the Kaulika initiation. || 676 ||
Having filled the mouth with the perfected substance (siddhadravya) combined with the nectar of the five products of the cow (pañcagavya), [one should proceed].
One should consecrate the beloved disciple; this is declared to be what is called the "mouthful" (gaṇḍuṣa).
With a conch or a water-pot filled with wine, joined with *sañjīva* fish, and completely full of the five nectars (*pañcāmṛta*). || 678 ||
Then one should perform the consecration with sprouts arising from the family tree (kulavṛkṣa). This is proclaimed here as the "Full Consecration" (pūrṇābhiṣeka) in the path of the Kula. || 679 ||
If Kaulikas die while deprived of the full consecration (pūrṇābhiṣeka), they attain the state of a Piśāca until the dissolution of all beings (ābhūtasamplava). || 680 ||
This initiation, performed by a preceptor according to the prescribed rite, instantly consumes hundreds of thousands of minor sins and tens of millions of major sins.
Just as iron, when pierced by the lord of juices (mercury), attains the state of gold.
For in this way, the self, pierced by initiation, swiftly attains the state of Śiva. || 682 ||
His karma having been burnt by the fire of initiation (dīkṣā), his bonds severed by Māyā, and having reached the supreme pinnacle of knowledge, he who is dispassionate becomes Śiva. (683)
The Śūdra-hood of the Śūdra has departed; the Brahmin-hood of the Brahmin has departed.
In one who is perfected through the purificatory rite of initiation, no distinction of caste exists.
A pedestal made of wood or stone, upon which a liṅga born of iron, clay, or precious gems is installed.
Just as Mahādeva is described, so too are the initiated members of the castes.
If an outcaste is initiated first and a twice-born person is initiated later, then,
according to the determination of the Kula scriptures, that outcaste is declared to be the elder.
And those who have been previously initiated by the Guru, the Śakti, or the sons [of the Guru] should be worshipped by him like the Guru;
they must never be treated with contempt. || 687 ||
In the Kaulika and Vāma paths, the initiation by piercing (vedhadīkṣā) bestows its fruit; other [initiations] belong to the Dakṣiṇa path, otherwise one would fall [from the path]. || 688 ||

That which was accomplished by the Guru, preceded by initiation and transmitted through the lineage, and that which is obtained by a worthy disciple from one who is worthy—that too will undoubtedly succeed. || 689 ||
One should recite the mantra for exactly one month, encased within the *bhūtalipi* (the alphabet).
By reciting it one thousand times, both in direct and reverse order, his mantra becomes perfected. || 690 ||
The mantra-practitioner should worship the maṇḍala, conjoined with the letters of the Mātṛkā.
Through both direct and reverse order, the mantra is perfected within six months.
Preceded by the syllables of the three principles (tritattva), and preceded by the syllables of the Mātṛkā.
Having recited it one hundred times both forwards and backwards, the mantra becomes perfected within a month.
By the mere recitation of the Mātṛkā, tens of millions upon tens of millions of mantras are recited; of this there is no doubt, for all reality arises from it. 693.
First there is birth-impurity (jāta-sūtaka) and at the end, death-impurity (mṛta-sūtaka). That mantra for which there is no preliminary rite (puraścaraṇa) will never be perfected. || 694 ||

When one whose limbs are nourished by another's food and drink performs an accumulation of merit, half of the fruit belongs to the giver of the food and half to the doer; of this there is no doubt. (695)
Adorned with fragrant flowers, ornaments, perfumes, and the like, success comes into his hands; it cannot be attained otherwise even in ten million lifetimes.
Established in that, with his life-breath directed toward that, his mind fixed on that, and having that as his supreme goal.
While contemplating that welfare of others, one should softly recite the mantra. || 697 ||
When weary from recitation, one should meditate again; when weary from meditation, one should recite again.
For one engaged in recitation, meditation, and so forth, the mantra is quickly accomplished. || 698 ||
Then the practitioner, possessing a pure heart and endowed with the observances, should proceed for the sake of the ritual application.
One should recite the mantra that bestows curses and favors one hundred thousand times according to the reality.
Then, in the consecrated fire, one should offer oblations with ten parts of rice grains mixed with sesame seeds and combined with the three sweets.
Furthermore, with perfumes, flowers, unbroken rice grains, ornaments, new garments, and so forth,
as well as with delightful family offerings such as various kinds of foods, edibles, meals, and drinks.
One should satisfy the circle of yoginīs according to the rule, in full detail.

Having thus performed the ritual placement (nyāsa), recitation (japa), meditation (dhyāna), along with oblations, worship, and libations, one should carry out the practical applications; there is no doubt that success will be attained.

At the conclusion of the ritual application, one should perform the worship of the wheel according to the prescribed rule. One should recite the mantra one hundred thousand times, accompanied by meditation and ritual placement (nyāsa). || 703 ||
For the sake of pacifying defects in the ritual application, and for the sake of one's own welfare alone.
It indicates the vowels, consonants, words, diphthongs, the bindu, and consciousness. || 704 ||

Having understood the short, long, and protracted vowels and so forth, one should accomplish the ritual acts. The root is the seed-syllable of the temple (Prāsāda-bīja), possessing the brilliant luster of the rising sun. || 705 ||
Upon the head is the supreme seed-syllable, possessing a radiance equal to ten thousand moons.
Filled with the bliss arising from the touch of each other's hands. || 706 ||
With uninterrupted luminosities extending from the base (mūlādhāra) up to the aperture of Brahmā (brahmarandhra).
One should constantly contemplate oneself as being drenched from head to foot with the supreme nectar-essence; such a person is not afflicted by ritual applications.
Now, for the benefit of the world, I shall explain meditation, recitation, and so forth, by which peace is produced when one's own illness or other afflictions arise. (708)
Having sat upon a soft seat, one should meditate, preceded by salutation to the Guru, [visualizing] the full orb of the moon reaching up to the crown of the head.
The supreme seed-syllable of the Śrīprāsāda, conjoined with the sixteenth vowel.
It was auspicious, white as pearls, crystal, camphor, the kunda flower, and the moon.
One should meditate upon oneself, or indeed upon the Self of another, as having a body drenched in nectar produced from the seed-syllable together with the moon. || 711 ||
When one, endowed with youthful radiance, worships the Maṇḍala with the supreme mantra of the Śrīprāsāda recited one thousand and eight times, [the deity is pleased]. || 712 ||
The fear born of untimely death, great diseases, old age, and mortality.
"O gods, it is our certainty that for him there shall never arise any occurrence of possession by planets, epilepsy, vetālas, ghosts, madness, or the like. (713)
Free from old age and disease, endowed with sons, grandsons, and other descendants, he shall live for more than a hundred years, honored by all human beings. || 714 ||

In cases of diseases such as fever and insanity, one should recite [the mantra] while meditating on the head; or else, one should meditate on it at the root of Brahmā’s knot (brahmagranthi) or in that specific location. 715.
In the case of a major disease, one should visualize it as pervading all limbs, as previously described.
At that very moment, all diseases come to peace; of this there is no doubt. || 716 ||
He who meditates upon the ten sense organs shall obtain perfection of the senses; he who constantly contemplates the head shall become free from old age and death. || 717 ||
Situated within the solar disc in the center of the pericarp of the heart-lotus.
The seed-syllable of supreme faith is like the rising sun. || 718 ||
Having thus enveloped the mantra with twenty tactile syllables, which possess the luster of the Japā flower, Bandhūka, vermilion, ruby, and lotus. (719)
One should thus contemplate oneself as endowed with the full bloom of youth, having made the three worlds into jewels by the shadow of the mass of one's own radiance. (720)
One should always recite the mantra one thousand and eight times over the mandala.
The gods, dānavas, gandharvas, siddhas, cāraṇas, and guhyakas.
Vidyādharas, sages, yakṣas, nāgas, and celestial nymphs; women.
Lions, tigers, serpents, elephants, and other such wicked beasts as well.
He brings [them] under his control without a doubt; how much more so humans and others? || 722 ||

He attains sovereignty here on earth as well as enjoyments in heaven and other such rewards; furthermore, by remembering and reciting [this mantra] over the head of anyone, that person quickly becomes submissive. || 723 ||
One should meditate upon that seed-syllable of Parā-prāsāda, situated in the center of the circle of fire within the lotus of the Mūlādhāra, resembling the fire at the end of an aeon.
But when enveloped by the ten pervasive syllables in reverse order, he himself becomes like the fire of time (kālānala), causing terror to all beings. || 725 ||
Facing the southeast and endowed with the radiance of youth,
one should recite the mantra of the mandala one thousand and eight times.
Those who cause harm, the cruel, and those who harbor groundless hatred;
[He destroys] elemental spirits, fierce planets, vetālas, piśācas, and brahmarākṣasas. || 727 ||

One should contemplate them as having fallen into the midst of that fire, yet not being consumed by the flames; in an instant, they go to destruction from all sides like moths. He upon whose head one should meditate on the seed-syllable (bīja) meets with death. 728.
With the excellent sacrificial fuel-sticks of khadira, śveta-mandāra, amṛtā, and bhānu;
Or else, it may be made from the wood of the jackfruit, fig, holy fig, plakṣa, or apāmārga trees.
Or with *nandyāvarta*, white lotuses, and *hayāri* flowers;
or with one of these, as mentioned in the preceding half-verse, combined with sesame and rice.
Or with foods mixed with the three sweets, or even with milk-rice (pāyasa).
One should perform [the rites] from one thousand up to ten thousand, according to the specific requirement.

For the accomplishment here of the previously mentioned recitation that is characterized by sattva, there is the peaceful rite (śāntika), the nourishing rite (pauṣṭika), their conjunction, and assistance within the sattvic state. || 732 ||
[It was adorned] with [flowers] produced from the kadamba, aśoka, bakula, punnāga, āmra, and madhūka trees.
[The paste] produced from the two types of campaka, pālāśa, pāṭala, śrī, and kapittha [flowers]. || 733 ||
With *mālatī*, jasmine, *jāti*, bandhūka, and red lotuses;
With *kumārī*, *aruṇa*, *mandāra*, *jātī*, *kunda*, *japā*, and so forth. || 734 ||
Also with ripe coconuts, plantains, grapes, sugarcane, and flattened rice.
With sandalwood, agallochum, camphor, gorocana, saffron, and so forth. || 735 ||
With other auspicious substances combined with water from *śamī* leaves and fruit.
The fire-oblation for the rājasa [nature] is performed as before with the verses recited in separate half-verses.

One may perform [the rites] from a thousand up to ten thousand according to the requirements of the task. Stambha (paralysis), vaśya (subjugation), mohana (delusion), and kautuka (curiosity) are considered to be of the nature of rajas. || 737 ||
With *nimbākṣa*, *bhāskara*, *unmatta*, *karavīra*, and *viṣadaṇḍi*; with black *kuṭaja* trees, and indeed with *agnikuṇḍa* and *ṛkṣavṛkṣaka* trees. (738)
Combined with house-soot, charcoal, poison, and potent toxins.
One should fashion an image of the enemy using the dust from the middle of his footprint, combined with funeral ashes and ground with the juice of the *unmatta* plant. (739)
Or whatever [is produced] from the field, trees, or wood of that mind.
One should suspend [the vessel] with its breath properly established over the sacrificial pit (kuṇḍa). || 740 ||
The mantra-practitioner, with a turbid mind, fierce gaze, and impatient wrath, should carve an image out of clay beneath the sacrificial pit according to the prescribed rite. || 741 ||
